title: Endothelial-specific Tie2 knockout mouse model - Tie2fl/fl;Cdh5-creERT2(+/-): a potent tool for inducible Tie2 deletion in vasculature across multiple organs.
abstract: TEK receptor tyrosine kinase (Tie2) is predominantly expressed on endothelial cells and is known to play a critical role in vascular development and stability. Due to its role in vascular development, germline knockout of Tie2 is embryonically lethal. In this study we aimed to generate an inducible Tie2 knockout mouse model that specifically targets the mature endothelium. Mice with floxed Tie2 exon 9 alleles (Tie2fl/fl) were crossed with heterozygous Cdh5-creERT2(+/-) mice to generate Tie2fl/fl;Cdh5-creERT2(+/-) (cTie2-KO) mice. Deletion of Tie2 in the endothelium of adult cTie2-KO mice was induced by intraperitoneal injection of tamoxifen, where Tie2fl/fl/Cre- (Tie2fl/fl) mice served as controls. Five weeks after the start of treatment, organs were evaluated for Tie2 deletion at the DNA, RNA, and protein level. Another set of organs were collected for immunocytochemical analysis, to visually assess the expression levels of Tie2 within the tissue vasculature. The functional effect of the loss of Tie2 on the vasculature was evaluated by measuring vascular permeability in all organs in a separate set of mice. Tie2 exon 9 was deleted at the DNA level in the brains of cTie2-KO mice. All organs in cTie2-KO mice showed a significant reduction in expression of Tie2 mRNA at multiple exon levels as compared to Tie2fl/fl controls. Total protein evaluation via ELISA showed a significant reduction of Tie2 in all tissue homogenates of cTie2-KO mice. Co-localization of Tie2 with a pan-endothelial marker demonstrated that Tie2 expression was lost in the microvascular segments of all organs evaluated, as compared to control mice. Notably, vascular permeability as measured by dextran extravasation was increased in the brain parenchyma of cTie2-KO mice as compared to control mice. Deletion of Tie2 did not affect peripheral organ permeability. We have successfully generated a Tie2 conditional knockout mouse with significant endothelial specific deletion across multiple organs. Furthermore, at baseline we see functional deficits in cTie2-KO mice that are related specifically to blood brain barrier permeability independent of permeability in peripheral organs. This mouse model holds promise for opportunities to investigate the role of Tie2 in multiple organ vasculatures in health and disease conditions.

title: Association of platelet count with incident motoric cognitive risk syndrome among Chinese adults aged 60 years or older: a national prospective cohort study.
abstract: Motoric cognitive risk syndrome (MCR), defined by subjective cognitive complaints and slow gait in individuals without dementia, is a clinically relevant pre-dementia phenotype. Platelets are increasingly linked to inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and neurovascular signaling, but the prospective association between platelet count and MCR remains unclear. To examine whether baseline platelet count is associated with incident MCR among older Chinese adults. We analyzed 2,246 participants aged 60 years or older from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study who were free of MCR at baseline in 2011 and had platelet count and follow-up MCR data in 2013. Platelet count was modeled as a continuous variable per 100 × 10⁹/L increase and by quintiles, with the middle quintile as the reference. Multivariable logistic regression models were adjusted for sociodemographic characteristics, lifestyle factors, adiposity indicators, depressive symptoms, and major chronic diseases. Restricted cubic spline analysis was used to evaluate the dose-response pattern. Subgroup analyses and a sensitivity analysis excluding participants with baseline stroke were also conducted. During the 2-year follow-up, 264 participants (11.8%) developed MCR. In the fully adjusted model, each 100 × 10⁹/L increase in platelet count was associated with higher odds of incident MCR (odds ratio [OR] = 1.25, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.06-1.47; P = 0.007). Compared with the middle quintile, the fourth and fifth quintiles showed increased odds of MCR (Q4: OR = 1.62, 95% CI: 1.05-2.50; Q5: OR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.14-2.69), whereas the lower quintiles were not statistically significant. Restricted cubic spline analysis indicated an overall association (P = 0.022) without clear evidence of non-linearity (P for non-linearity = 0.402). The association persisted after excluding participants with baseline stroke, and no statistically significant subgroup interactions were observed. Among Chinese adults aged 60 years or older, higher baseline platelet count was prospectively associated with increased odds of incident MCR. Platelet count may represent a readily measured hematologic correlate of incident MCR; however, the observational design precludes causal or predictive interpretation. Studies with longer follow-up and platelet activation, inflammatory, coagulation, and neuroimaging markers are needed to clarify the underlying mechanisms. Not applicable.

title: INTENSIFY-a randomized, controlled trial to investigate the effect of an early intensified pharmacological treatment for major psychiatric disorders after treatment failure in the current episode: a study protocol.
abstract: Schizophrenia, bipolar depression and major depressive disorders collectively affect over 10 million people across the European Union and are associated with annual healthcare and societal costs of more than 600 billion euros. When diagnosed, patients are usually prescribed psychotropic medication. A substantial proportion of patients insufficiently responds to first- and second-line treatments, which is termed as treatment resistance. While third-line treatments are relatively effective in TR conditions, it remains unclear whether providing these treatments in an earlier phase provides benefits. INTENSIFY consists of three international, multicenter, controlled, randomized, open-label trials, with a treatment duration of 6 weeks. After failure of a first-line treatment in the current episode, 1254 participants will be recruited by at least 16 sites and randomized to either a third-line treatment (early intensified pharmacological treatment) or treatment as usual (standard second-line treatment). Adult participants (age ≥ 18yrs) with a diagnosis of schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder or schizophreniform disorder, major depressive disorder, or bipolar depression are eligible after a treatment failure in the current episode due to lack of efficacy. The primary objective is to compare change in symptom severity after 6 weeks. The secondary objective is to compare the two treatment arms on changes of severity symptoms, cognitive function, quality of life, functional measures, digital mental health markers, side effects and concomitant medication. ANCOVA analyses will be performed. Should the current study show clinical evidence that the use of third-line treatment is efficacious and safe earlier to treat severe mental illness, the results could impact treatment guidelines in due course. In addition, the study will contribute to the identification of clinical, digital and blood-based markers that are associated with treatment response to early and intensified treatments. The trials are registered in www. gov under numbers NCT05603104 (merged study protocol; study center in Israel) and under the numbers for the split protocols NCT05958875 (SZ), NCT05973786 (BD) and NCT05973851 (MDD) for the EU and UK sites. The study is registered in the Australian and New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry under Registration number ACTRN12625000327482 (SZ), ACTRN12625000328471 (BD) and ACTRN12625000329460 (MDD). Registered on April 17, 2025.

title: Understanding cerebral autoregulation and cerebrovascular reactivity: mechanistic perspectives and clinical insights from TBI.
abstract: Cerebrovascular reactivity and cerebral blood flow autoregulation are critical determinants of brain homeostasis but are often conflated in clinical practice. Although these constructs are closely related and arise from vascular responses to vasoactive stimuli, they reflect distinct physiological responses and measurement approaches: autoregulation is assessed through changes in cerebral blood flow, and pressure reactivity through changes in cerebral blood volume. A fundamental clinical challenge is that the full autoregulatory curve is rarely observable in an individual patient at a single point in time; consequently, isolated measurements from classical assessments or continuous indices such as the pressure reactivity index (PRx), mean flow index (Mx), and arterial mean flow index (Mxa) are each associated with different components of cerebrovascular physiology, providing only partial views of cerebrovascular function and frequently yielding apparently conflicting results. This Review addresses a central clinical question: can multimodal neuromonitoring help determine where a patient is operating on the autoregulatory curve? We synthesise current understanding of the physiological relationships among cerebral perfusion pressure, cerebral blood flow, and cerebral blood volume, and examine the mechanisms underlying divergent autoregulatory index behaviour. By integrating mechanistic physiological schematics and representative clinical cases, we propose an objective educational framework that links classical cerebrovascular physiology with contemporary bedside monitoring. Within this framework, six conceptual physiological zones are delineated. These zones demonstrate how variations in vascular tone, intracranial compliance, and critical closing pressure shape autoregulatory responses generate differing patterns in PRx, Mx, and Mxa. Fully defining a patient's complex cerebrovascular state requires looking beyond any single parameter. Together, PRx, Mx, and Mxa provide complementary information, where discordant findings may represent distinct physiological mechanisms rather than measurement error. Interpreting these indices together within a mechanistic framework may improve identification of a patient's position along the autoregulatory curve, support more consistent bedside interpretation, and ultimately facilitate personalised cerebral perfusion pressure management.

title: Evaluation of oxidative stress level: total antioxidant capacity, malondialdehyde and superoxide dismutase activity in children with pneumonia compared to healthy children.
abstract: Viral pneumonia is a leading cause of death in young children worldwide. Oxidant/antioxidant imbalance has been reported in various infectious diseases. This study aimed to evaluate oxidative stress and antioxidant defense markers - specifically malondialdehyde (MDA), total antioxidant capacity (TAC), and superoxide dismutase (SOD) - in children hospitalized with pneumonia compared to healthy controls. This case-control study included 53 children aged 2 to 10 years: 27 children with pneumonia and 26 healthy controls. Plasma MDA, SOD, and TAC levels were measured using ELISA kits (Kiazist Company, Iran). Blood samples were collected at the time of hospitalization. A researcher-designed checklist recorded demographic information (age, sex, weight, and BMI). Data were analyzed using SPSS version 14 software. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. MDA and SOD levels in the pneumonia group (2.49 ± 0.52 µmol/L and 3.47 ± 0.69 U/mL, respectively) were significantly higher than those in the control group (1.63 ± 0.34 µmol/L and 1.33 ± 0.20 U/mL, respectively) (p < 0.001). Conversely, TAC levels in the pneumonia group (0.88 ± 0.18 mmol/L) were significantly lower than those in the control group (1.69 ± 0.21 mmol/L) (p < 0.001). Pneumonia in children is associated with increased oxidative stress and decreased systemic antioxidant capacity. These findings suggest that redox imbalance may play a role in the pathophysiology of the disease; however, causal relationships and therapeutic implications remain to be confirmed, as interventional and longitudinal studies are lacking. Antioxidant modulation may warrant further investigation as an adjunctive therapy.

title: Peripheral molecular signatures of major depressive disorder: a systematic review of blood-derived biomarkers for diagnosis, stratification, and treatment response.
abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is biologically heterogeneous, yet diagnosis and treatment selection remain largely symptom-based. Blood-derived molecular biomarkers may offer scalable tools for biomarker discovery, biological stratification, and treatment-response research, but their clinical readiness remains uncertain. This PRISMA-compliant systematic review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261379864). PubMed, Scopus, and Embase were searched from 2014 to 27 April 2026 for human studies evaluating blood-derived molecular biomarkers in MDD or clinically defined depressive phenotypes with extractable depression-relevant data. Eligible domains included transcriptomics, DNA methylation, non-coding RNA, immune-inflammatory, mitochondrial/metabolic, neurotrophic/neuroendocrine, multi-omics, and machine-learning biomarker studies. Owing to methodological and platform heterogeneity, a structured narrative synthesis was performed rather than quantitative meta-analysis. Methodological quality was assessed using a modified QUADOMICS framework, prediction-model studies were additionally assessed using PROBAST, and certainty was judged using a modified GRADE approach. Of 9,354 records identified, 25 reports met the eligibility criteria, representing 24 independent participant datasets because two methylation analyses used the same underlying NESDA cohort. Included studies used whole blood, PBMCs, leukocytes, monocytes, serum, plasma, and cell-free RNA across diverse molecular platforms. Individual biomarkers were heterogeneous, but recurrent pathway-level signals involved immune-inflammatory and interferon-related pathways, NF-κB signalling, mitochondrial and energy metabolism, DNA methylation and epigenetic regulation, neurodevelopmental/synaptic pathways, stress-response signalling, autophagy, and non-coding RNA regulation. Multi-marker and multi-omics panels showed promising apparent diagnostic or treatment-response relevance, but most were internally validated, cohort-specific, or exploratory. Modified GRADE certainty was low to very low across biomarker domains. Blood-derived molecular signatures in MDD show stronger convergence at the pathway level than at the individual-biomarker level. Current evidence supports hypothesis generation and biological stratification, but no blood-derived biomarker or panel is ready for routine diagnosis or treatment selection.

title: The serotonin axis in cancer: metabolism, epigenetics, and immune regulation.
abstract: The serotonin axis, encompassing the biosynthesis, transport, receptor signaling and metabolism of serotonin, has emerged as a context-dependent regulatory network implicated in cancer biology. Beyond its classical neurotransmitter functions, serotonin modulates tumor progression through receptor-dependent signaling pathways and non-canonical mechanisms such as histone serotonylation, which directly links cellular metabolism to epigenetic regulation. Available evidence suggests that these processes can influence tumor cell proliferation, metabolic adaptation, plasticity and therapeutic drug resistance. Furthermore, the serotonin axis plays a context-dependent role in shaping the tumor microenvironment by regulating the functions of T cells, macrophages and other stromal components, thereby influencing responses to cancer immunotherapy. These diverse regulatory mechanisms have prompted the development of therapeutic strategies targeting serotonin biosynthesis and metabolism, serotonin transport, receptor signaling, and serotonylation, although their efficacy remains highly context-dependent. We further discuss emerging mechanistic insights, unresolved questions, and the opportunities and challenges for developing context-dependent therapeutic strategies targeting this axis.

title: Dorsomedial prefrontal cortex repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with antidepressants in major depressive disorder: a randomized, double-blind, single-center, sham-controlled trial.
abstract: Dorsomedial prefrontal cortex repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (DMPFC-rTMS) has shown some evidence of an antidepressant effect. This study aimed to examine the efficacy and safety of DMPFC-rTMS as a combination strategy with concurrently initiated selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) compared with conventional high-frequency left-prefrontal rTMS (HF-rTMS) + SSRI or sham stimulation + SSRI. In this prospective, single-center, six-week, randomized, three-arm, double-blind, sham- and active-comparator-controlled trial, patients with a current episode of major depressive disorder (MDD) were randomly allocated in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive either DMPFC-rTMS (20 sessions, 110% motor threshold, 2000 pulses), HF-rTMS (20 sessions, 110% motor threshold, 2000 pulses), or sham stimulation, all in combination with a concurrently initiated SSRI. The primary outcome was the change in the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) score at week six of the study. The secondary outcomes included changes in subjective assessment; response, remission, and dropout rates; and side effects of both rTMS and antidepressant treatment. Sixty patients (20 per group) were randomized and included in the analysis. The mean change in the MADRS total score from baseline to week 6 was -14.3 points (95% confidence interval [CI]: -18.3, -10.3) in the DMPFC-rTMS group, -8.2 points (95% CI: -11.7, -4.7) in the HF-rTMS group, and -12.6 points (95% CI: -16.1, -9.0) in the sham group. However, no pairwise comparisons between these groups reached statistical significance. The response/remission rates (DMPFC-rTMS: 35%/20%; HF-rTMS: 30%/15%; sham: 55%/45%) and the dropout rates (45%, 25%, and 25%, respectively) did not differ significantly between the groups. No serious adverse events occurred. This study did not demonstrate superior efficacy of DMPFC-rTMS or HF-rTMS over sham stimulation when initiated concurrently with SSRIs. These findings should be interpreted as exploratory. The trial was underpowered to detect the likely incremental effect of adding rTMS to a concurrently initiated SSRI and was further limited by a high sham response and differential attrition in the DMPFC-rTMS arm. Optimal stimulation parameters and patient selection require further validation. ISRCTN26184028 (Registered retrospectively, July 26, 2022).

title: Comparison of the anaesthetic efficacy and safety of different doses of esketamine combined with propofol in hysteroscopic surgery: a randomised, double-blind controlled trial.
abstract: Hysteroscopy is increasingly performed under day-surgery total intravenous anaesthesia, but propofol alone provides insufficient analgesia and the routine adjunct of opioids is associated with respiratory depression and emetic complications. Esketamine, the S-enantiomer of ketamine, offers analgesia together with sympathomimetic support and represents a promising opioid-sparing alternative; however, its optimal dose for combination with propofol in this setting has not been firmly established. In this prospective, randomised, double-blind, controlled trial, 160 women aged 18-60 years (ASA I-II) scheduled for elective hysteroscopy were assigned to four groups using computer-generated random numbers: K1 (esketamine 0.15 mg/kg), K2 (esketamine 0.3 mg/kg), K3 (esketamine 0.5 mg/kg) or S (sufentanil 0.1 µg/kg). All patients received an induction dose of propofol 1.5 mg/kg followed by maintenance infusion of 4-6 mg·kg⁻¹·h⁻¹. The primary outcomes were postoperative pain (Numeric Rating Scale, NRS) and total intra-operative propofol consumption; secondary outcomes were perioperative haemodynamics, recovery time and adverse events. After exclusion of three patients with major protocol deviation, 157 patients were analysed (K1 = 40, K2 = 38, K3 = 40, S = 39). Demographics, surgical and anaesthesia times were comparable between groups. NRS scores at 10 and 30 min post-recovery were significantly lower in groups K2, K3 and S than in group K1 (p < 0.001). Mean arterial pressure at the start of surgery (T2, immediately after the start of surgery) and at the end of surgery (T3) was significantly higher in K1 than in the other three groups (p < 0.001). Total propofol consumption did not differ between groups (p = 0.95). The incidence of intra-operative hypertension was significantly greater in K1 (22.5%) than in K2 (0%), K3 (5.0%) and S (5.1%) (p = 0.002), and the incidence of SpO₂ < 90% was significantly greater in S (20.5%) than in K1 (0%), K2 (5.3%) and K3 (5.0%) (p = 0.004). The incidence of emergence agitation differed among groups, with the highest incidence observed in K3 (10.0%) (p = 0.034). Among the regimens tested, esketamine 0.3 mg/kg combined with propofol 1.5 mg/kg was associated with a favourable balance of analgesia, haemodynamic stability and safety. The 0.15 mg/kg dose was associated with higher postoperative pain scores and a higher incidence of intra-operative hypertension, while 0.5 mg/kg was associated with a higher incidence of agitation and a longer recovery time without additional analgesic benefit at 30 min. All three esketamine doses were associated with a lower incidence of hypoxaemia than the sufentanil regimen. The trial was registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400092022) with the retrospective registration date 2024/11/07.

title: Susceptibility haplotypes in non-cystic fibrosis newborns with elevated immunoreactive trypsinogen.
abstract: Cystic fibrosis (CF) represents the most prevalent life-threatening autosomal recessive disorder in Europe, primarily affecting the respiratory tract, exocrine pancreatic function, and lipid metabolism. Immunoreactive trypsinogen (IRT) quantification constitutes the first-tier test in neonatal CF screening programs; however, elevated IRT levels may also be detected in infants who do not develop CF, generating false-positive (FP) results. The biological basis underlying increased IRT in these cases remains poorly understood and may involve genetic determinants independent of CFTR. Dried blood spot (DBS) samples were collected from full-term neonates with normal growth parameters, classified as true negatives (TN) or FP through CF newborn screening programs across multiple European centers. IRT levels were measured via standardized immunoassay, and genomic DNA extracted from DBS underwent whole-exome sequencing (WES). Bioinformatic analyses integrated functional prediction, evolutionary conservation, and allele frequency data, with variant prioritization restricted to a curated panel of genes implicated in pancreatic disease. Following quality control, 212 samples (94 FP, 118 TN) were included. Comparative analyses identified significant enrichment of variants in five genes among FP subjects. Notably, top loci localized to regulatory regions and genes involved in oxidative stress, suggesting a mechanistic link with pancreatic inflammation and elevated IRT. Several variants clustered within high linkage disequilibrium regions, supporting the presence of susceptibility haplotypes. Burden testing of rare variants confirmed significant associations for CFTR, PRSS1, and PRSS2 after multiple testing corrections. These results suggest that genetic variation beyond CFTR is associated with elevated neonatal IRT in infants without CF and support further investigation of pancreatic-related pathways in false-positive CF newborn screening.

title: Supportive Environmental Design for Post-stroke Rehabilitation: A Participatory Concept Mapping Study.
abstract: PurposeTo explore home and neighborhood environment aspects that support post-stroke rehabilitation.BackgroundThe design of healthcare environments influences rehabilitation outcomes, however, evidence for outpatient contexts, particularly the home and neighborhood remain limited.MethodWe used descriptive statistics and cluster analysis to explore stakeholders' perspectives on environmental factors that support rehabilitation and to identify patterns in how environmental features were organized and rated.ResultsSeveral home and nearby environmental features were clustered around engagement in rehabilitation and participation in everyday activities. Patterns suggested that accessibility, proximity to routine services, and opportunities for social contact tended to co-occur with higher perceived support for rehabilitation.ConclusionsThe immediate environment appears to play a role in community-based recovery after stroke, with design, social context, and care processes intertwined. The findings highlight that many feasible actions such as strengthening communication, ensuring adaptive home environments, and improving neighborhood accessibility can help align housing and local planning with everyday rehabilitation after stroke. While recognizing the exploratory nature of the findings, architectural planners and healthcare practitioners could draw on these insights to inform housing planning and more inclusive environments.

title: Median effective infusion rate (ED50) of continuous cisatracurium for preserving interpretable TceMEP signals during intraspinal tumor resection: a prospective up-and-down sequential allocation study.
abstract: Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring (IONM), particularly transcranial electrical stimulation motor evoked potentials (TceMEP), plays a crucial role in preserving motor function during intraspinal tumor resection. However, neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBAs) may attenuate TceMEP signals and complicate reliable monitoring. Partial neuromuscular blockade (pNMB) through continuous NMBA infusion may help balance interpretable TceMEP monitoring with acceptable surgical conditions. This study aimed to evaluate the interpretability of TceMEP signals during continuous cisatracurium infusion and thereby estimate the median effective infusion rate (ED50) associated with preservation of interpretable TceMEP signals during intraspinal tumor resection. Twenty-seven patients undergoing elective intraspinal tumor resection with TceMEP monitoring were enrolled in this prospective, single-center, open-label, sequential dose-finding study using Dixon's up-and-down method. After a standard intubation dose of cisatracurium, continuous infusion was started at 1.0 µg/(kg·min). TceMEP signal interpretability was used as the binary response variable for sequential allocation. A neurophysiologist blinded to the infusion rate classified the signals as interpretable or uninterpretable; the anesthesiology team was not blinded because dose adjustment was required by the sequential design. The infusion rate for each subsequent patient was increased or decreased by a factor of 1.2 according to the response in the preceding patient. ED50 and its 95% confidence interval (CI) were estimated using Dixon's method. The estimated ED50 of continuous cisatracurium infusion associated with preservation of interpretable TceMEP signals was 1.65 µg/(kg·min) (95% CI, 1.52-1.79 µg/(kg·min)). No clinically significant patient movement or serious infusion-related adverse events were observed during the study. In patients undergoing intraspinal tumor resection with TceMEP monitoring, the median effective infusion rate of continuous cisatracurium associated with preservation of interpretable TceMEP signals was 1.65 µg/(kg·min). This value should be interpreted as an ED50 estimate rather than a recommended maximum acceptable infusion rate. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2200057610. Registered on March 15, 2022, before enrollment of the first participant.

title: Central Thyroid Hormone Receptor-Beta Agonist Selectively Inhibits Voluntary Alcohol Consumption in Mice.
abstract: Decades of prior work have indicated associations between thyroid hormone axis dysregulation and alcohol use disorder (AUD). Specifically, disruptions in thyroid hormone levels are related to altered mood, compulsion, craving, and relapse in patients with AUD. Likewise, modulating thyroid hormones in preclinical models can impact ethanol (EtOH) consumption. Recently, we have shown that daily treatment with central nervous system selective thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist, Sob-AM2, can reduce daily EtOH consumption and preference in male and female C57BL6/J mice at a 1.0 mg/kg dose. However, it is unclear if lower doses can attain reductions in drinking and if the effects of Sob-AM2 habituate with chronic dosing over time. Furthermore, as thyroid hormone signaling within the brain can influence many behaviors, the precise mechanisms driving Sob-AM2's influence on EtOH drinking remain unclear. In the present study, we tested if treatment with a lower dose of Sob-AM2, 0.3 mg/kg, for 9 days would be sufficient to reduce EtOH intake and preference and if these effects would be sustained over a two-week period. In addition, we tested whether the effects of Sob-AM2 are exerted via altering ETOH elimination from blood, influencing caloric consumption, affecting taste for sucrose, or altering avoidance of a bitter tastant. We found that Sob-AM2 treatment for 9 days was sufficient to reduce both EtOH intake and preference while increasing water and total fluid intake, and these effects were also present at 23 days of treatment. Meanwhile, treatment with Sob-AM2 did not result in alterations of EtOH elimination rate, nor did it affect food consumption, sucrose consumption, or quinine avoidance in a way that explains reductions in EtOH consumption. These results demonstrate that agonism of central thyroid hormone receptor-beta selectively decreases voluntary EtOH consumption and may indicate a promising novel therapeutic approach for the treatment of AUD.

title: Integration of genome-wide association study and single-cell transcriptome analysis reveals the role of N6-methyladenosine in treatment resistance in lung cancer.
abstract: Platinum-based chemotherapy resistance, particularly to carboplatin, is a major challenge in the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation, which regulates gene and protein expression by influencing numerous aspects of mRNA metabolism, has been implicated in NSCLC pathogenesis, but its role in treatment resistance remains unclear. We performed an innovative integrated analysis by combining genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics, methylation quantitative trait loci (mQTL) data, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from NSCLC patients. First, a transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) using FUSION analysis was conducted to identify associations between m6A methylation sites, genes, and NSCLC by integrating m6A methylation profiles with GWAS summary statistics. Subsequently, scRNA-seq data were used to characterize NSCLC epithelial cell subpopulations and dynamically delineate the transition from treatment-sensitive to treatment-resistant states. Finally, a cross-omics correlation network was constructed by integrating the m6A and scRNA-seq datasets to identify associations between dynamic m6A modifications and carboplatin resistance. Our integrated analysis identified 6 m6A sites and 9 genes significantly associated with NSCLC. ScRNA-seq analysis revealed a significant increase in the proportion of epithelial cells in the carboplatin-resistant group. Marker genes of these carboplatin-resistant epithelial cells were enriched in pathways related to glutathione metabolism, ferroptosis, and endoplasmic reticulum protein processing. The RAS oncogene family member RAB7A was identified as a critical driver of treatment resistance. MeRIP-qPCR confirmed that RAB7A mRNA carries m6A modifications, and RIP-qPCR demonstrated direct binding of the m6A reader IGF2BP2 to RAB7A transcripts. Functional assays showed that RAB7A overexpression significantly increased intracellular glutathione levels and reduced lipid ROS, indicating enhanced antioxidant capacity and ferroptosis suppression. RAB7A expression was significantly upregulated in NSCLC patients with a poor response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Functional validation in vitro confirmed that overexpression of RAB7A conferred carboplatin resistance in NSCLC cells. This study establishes a novel paradigm in which m6A-mediated gene regulation is a key contributor to chemoresistance. Furthermore, we identify RAB7A as a functionally relevant gene associated with carboplatin resistance, warranting further investigation as a candidate therapeutic target.

title: External validation of the Liverpool Head Injury Tomography Score for mild traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Mild Traumatic Brain Injury (mTBI) neurosurgical referrals are increasing. This study aimed to externally validate a radiological scoring system to define a 'neurosurgically significant' mild TBI and evaluate its impact on referral outcome if implemented. Retrospective, external validation of the UK Liverpool Head Injury Tomography Score (LIV-HITS). Consecutive neurosurgery referrals to a tertiary neurosurgery centre for mild TBI were included (1st January 2022-30th June 2022). Mechanism of injury, LIV-HITS and management decision were identified, and diagnostic accuracy determined. A total of 1547 referrals were included. 147 (9.5%) were accepted for transfer, and 1400 (90.5%) were designated as local management. For neurosurgical transfer, the sensitivity of LIV-HITS was 99.3% and the specificity was 43.9%, with a positive predictive value of 15.7%, and negative predictive value of 99.8%. Discriminatory power of the model was fair (AUC 0.71, 95% CI 0.66-0.76). In 6 months, the score identified 615 referrals (39.8%) that could have been successfully triaged to local management if the scoring system was used. The LIV-HITS has a sensitivity of over 99% for excluding a neurosurgically significant mild TBI in an externally validated cohort. However, the discriminatory power of the score is poor for stratifying which patients eventually get transferred to a neurosurgical centre. The score in clinical practice could be used as a 'rule out' tool for mild TBI referrals, whilst identifying potentially significant mild TBI that would warrant emergency neurosurgical consideration.

title: Transcriptional profiling of antidepressant ketamine and electroconvulsive therapy treatment.
abstract: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) affects 30-50% of patients with major depressive disorder (MDD). Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and sub-anesthetic ketamine treatment can relieve TRD, yet their antidepressant mechanisms remain unclear. We hypothesized that peripheral blood gene expression might offer a non-invasive proxy of potential treatment-response biomarkers. We conducted a transcriptome analysis on peripheral blood samples from individuals with TRD undergoing ECT (N = 37) or serial ketamine infusions (N = 60), and non-depressed controls (N = 35). Samples were collected at baseline and at multiple follow-up time points. Differential gene expression (DGE) at the single gene and network level identified transcriptional changes and co-regulated gene modules associated with diagnosis, treatment, and response/remission status using Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), correcting for multiple comparisons. Longitudinal transcriptional changes were not detected for either treatment for individual genes or networks (FDR corrected or |logFC| >0.05). When comparing remitters and non-remitters at baseline in the ketamine group, we observed evidence of enrichment for immune-related functions overall with one gene significantly differentially expressed (i.e., IGKV1-9) (p = 2.5E-05, logFC = -0.51). In the ECT sample, when considering gene networks, we observed significant interaction effects between time and diagnosis. At least six co-regulated gene modules yielded significant differences at baseline between ECT patients and controls. Despite the robust clinical improvements associated with ECT and ketamine, peripheral blood RNA-seq revealed only limited longitudinal gene expression changes. However, pre-treatment differences in gene expression profiles suggest some potential predictive value. Larger samples may be warranted to detect possible peripheral molecular signatures of rapid-acting antidepressant response.

title: Top-down semantic predictions align phonetic neuronal dynamics in human superior temporal gyrus.
abstract: Speech processing involves a hierarchy of cognitive layers from low-level phonetic to high-level semantic representations. However, interactions are not only feed-forward; feedback mechanisms are crucial for real-time, accurate speech recognition. Yet how distant levels interface during speech processing remains unclear. Here, we analyzed intracortical recordings from 624 neurons across three human participants implanted with microelectrode arrays in the anterior superior temporal gyrus during an auditory semantic categorization task and natural speech perception. We identified distinct neural subspaces, or manifolds, for lexico-semantic and phonetic features, with a functional separation of the corresponding low-dimensional dynamics. We contrasted a bottom-up cumulative and a top-down semantic hypothesis on phonetic-semantic temporal alignment, and found phonetic alignment to word-level semantic representations, signaling top-down prediction. These effects were consistent across participants at the spiking level, and remained undetected in adjacent ECoG recordings. These findings demonstrate the reorganization of neuronal population dynamics supporting phonetic representations during semantic prediction.

title: A model of brain function to predict tau across Alzheimer's disease and related disorders.
abstract: We developed a machine learning framework grounded in a computational model of brain function and FDG-PET imaging to predict Alzheimer's disease (AD)-type tau across AD and related disorders (ADRD). The model was trained on 1088 research participants spanning normal aging and ADRD with FDG-PET and flortaucipir-PET (FTP-PET). Validation was conducted in: (1) a longitudinal subset of the training cohort (n = 215), (2) Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (n = 295), and (3) a heretogeneous clinical cohort (n = 264; n = 28 with FTP-PET). Results showed that the model accurately predicted FTP-PET when applied at the participant-level (R2 ~ 0.34-0.71). It performed well in clinical scenarios, including classification of low versus high tau stages (79-95% accuracy) and prediction of tau in a heterogeneous clinical cohort without FTP-PET. These findings advance the understanding of the relationship between neurodegeneration and AD-type tau and provide a framework for estimating AD-type tau across ADRD.

title: Brain-Derived Neurotrophic Factor (BDNF), Estrogen Receptors, and Mossy Cells.
abstract: Dentate gyrus (DG) function depends on the neurotrophin brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) which shows robust synthesis in the principal cells, the granule cells (GCs). However, BDNF protein is present in the inner molecular layer (IML), where most afferents to GCs are from hilar mossy cells (MCs). Therefore, we asked whether MCs express BDNF mRNA and protein. Using adult mice, we found that MC BDNF mRNA and protein were expressed in the majority of MC somata and few other hilar neurons. Interestingly, IML BDNF was significantly greater in the ventral compared to dorsal DG. Additionally, dorsal IML BDNF was significantly higher in females on proestrous morning, when serum levels of estrogen peak, relative to metestrous morning, when estrogen is lower. Consistent with this observation, ventral MC somata, which project to the dorsal IML, showed more BDNF mRNA on proestrous morning than metestrous morning. Next, we asked if strong IML BDNF protein expression on proestrous morning was due to estrogen action at estrogen receptors (ERs) because estrogen binding to ERs can increase BDNF synthesis. We found that MCs have high expression of all ERs: ERα, ERβ and GPER1 in both sexes. When sexes were pooled, the percent of MCs labeled by ERβ and GPER1 exceeded the percent of MCs expressing ERα. When proestrous females were examined, GPER1-labeled MCs were greater than MCs labeled by ERα. The results demonstrate robust MC somatic expression of BDNF, relatively high ventral IML expression of BDNF, and estrous cycle dependence. The results also highlight robust MC ER expression, especially ERβ and GPER1, making the hilus a previously underestimated site of estrogen and BDNF action.

title: Neostigmine-induced Takotsubo cardiomyopathy: A rare cause of perioperative cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TTC) is a rare entity but can be life-threatening if not managed appropriately. Perioperative TTC is an extremely rare condition. We successfully managed a 26-year-old female patient who had TTC due to neostigmine during the perioperative period.

title: Lived experiences of methamphetamine users in Sri Lanka: A qualitative study on initiation, continuation, and barriers to abstinence.
abstract: Methamphetamine use is an emerging public health concern in Sri Lanka, yet there is limited qualitative understanding of the psychosocial and cognitive factors underlying its initiation, continuation, and barriers to abstinence. To explore the lived experiences of metha-mphetamine users in Sri Lanka, focusing on pathways to initiation, drivers of use, barriers to cessation, and perceived treatment needs. A qualitative study was conducted among 37 individuals attending substance use and psychiatric services at the National Hospital of Sri Lanka. Participants were recruited using purposive sampling, and in-depth semi-structured interviews were conducted until data saturation was achieved. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's framework. Measures to ensure trustworthiness included investigator triangulation, reflexivity, and systematic theme development. Three overarching themes were identified: socially mediated initiation, perceived functional enhancement and psychological reinforcement, entrapment, harm, and barriers to abstinence. Initiation was largely socially mediated, driven by peer influence, curiosity, and emotional distress. Continued use was reinforced by perceived functional enhancement, including improved energy, productivity, and sexual performance, despite progressive psychological and physical harm. A transition from initial euphoria to paranoia, low mood, and functional decline was commonly described. Persistent cognitive distortions, including beliefs in self-medication and functional benefits, contributed to ongoing use. Barriers to abstinence included craving, motivational ambivalence, social influences, and easy availability. Misconceptions regarding treatment, including the use of other subs-tances, were also evident. Methamphetamine use in Sri Lanka is sustained by a complex interplay of social exposure, psychological vulnerability, and cognitive distortions regarding perceived benefits. Addressing these factors requires culturally appropriate psychoeducation, early identification, and expansion of evidence-based psychosocial interventions within existing addiction treatment services.

title: The Effect of Perioperative Video Interventions on Postoperative Pain Control: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Postoperative pain is a major cause of suffering and is linked to serious complications, including delayed wound healing, increased cardiovascular risk, delayed rehabilitation, and chronic postsurgical pain. Modifiable psychological factors influence pain outcomes, and preliminary evidence suggests video interventions can reduce preoperative anxiety and improve patient satisfaction. We hypothesized that video interventions could improve postoperative pain control. Therefore, the aim of the current systematic review was to summarize all previous research and investigate the effects of perioperative video interventions on pain levels and/or analgesic consumption. The review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD42024596389) and followed the PRISMA Guidelines. We searched PubMed, EMBASE, CINAHL, Academic Search, and the Cochrane Central register of controlled trials from inception to October 2025 for randomized controlled trials in adult surgical patients. Trials assessing any perioperative video interventions reporting on postoperative pain intensity and/or analgesic consumption were included. Data was extracted independently by two authors, and data synthesis was qualitative due to significant heterogeneity. Risk of bias was assessed using the Revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials (RoB 2). Forty-four trials were included. Of the 42 trials assessing pain, 11 (26%) reported significantly lower pain in the intervention group. Of the 19 trials measuring analgesic consumption, eight (42%) reported significantly lower consumption in the intervention group. Only two trials demonstrated a benefit for both co-primary outcomes. Significant improvements in secondary outcomes, including anxiety, physical function, and satisfaction, were reported in 26 trials. Most trials were judged as having a high risk of bias. The current systematic review suggests that perioperative video interventions may improve acute postoperative pain control, although effects are inconsistent across trials. Future research should focus on identifying patient and intervention characteristics that predict efficacy to guide clinical implementation. This trustworthy systematic review presents an overview of current research findings for application of perioperative video-based treatments as part of managing postoperative pain. While this approach shows promise, more definitive evidence may be needed to justify more widespread implementation.

title: Sng as a distinct pain phenotype after minimally invasive spine surgery: Implications for analgesic use and recovery outcomes.
journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
abstract: Chronic postsurgical pain (CPSP) remains a major clinical challenge due to its heterogeneous pathophysiology and variable response to current analgesics. Sng (), a culture-specific sensory term used by Chinese-speaking patients to describe acid-like muscle soreness alongside pain, has been identified as a distinct dimension of chronic pain with unique underlying mechanisms and limited responsiveness to current therapies. This study proposed a CPSP phenotyping framework according to the presence and predominance of sng and non-sng components and evaluated the association of sng with clinical outcomes and analgesic utilization. Two independent retrospective cohorts were analyzed, including patients who underwent minimally invasive spine surgery (MISS) and who underwent vertebroplasty for osteoporotic vertebral compression fracture (OVCF). One-year postoperative patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and pharmacological burden quantified by the Medication Quantification Scale (MQS), were compared among four pain phenotypes: no CPSP, non-sng, sng, and mixed. In the MISS cohort, 72 patients had resolved pain and 207 had CPSP, including 30 (14.5%) with non-sng-dominant, 91 (44.0%) with sng-dominant, and 86 (41.5%) with mixed phenotypes. In the OVCF cohort, 39 patients had resolved pain and 78 had CPSP after vertebroplasty, including 5 (6.4%) with non-sng-dominant, 46 (59.0%) with sng-dominant, and 27 (34.6%) with mixed phenotypes. In both cohorts, sng-related phenotypes, particularly the mixed phenotype, were associated with poorer clinical outcomes, longer medication use, and greater pharmacological burden. Sng represents a major component of CPSP, and incorporating sng into CPSP phenotyping may facilitate mechanism-based, phenotype-specific management strategies.

title: Corrigendum to "SleepEEGpy: a Python-based software integration package to organize preprocessing, analysis, and visualization of sleep EEG data" [Comput. Biol. Med. 192, (2025), 110232].
Electrodiagnostic Classification of Sensory Neuropathies: Severity Clusters and Clinical Correlates.
abstract: Grading sensory neuropathy severity on nerve conduction studies (NCS) is operator dependent, which limits comparisons across patients, laboratories, and studies. We aimed to develop an objective severity classification to standardize NCS reporting and support clinical decision-making. We retrospectively analyzed NCS performed at IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital (2018-2024), extracted with a validated parser. Adult studies with sensory involvement were selected using sural sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitude thresholds after excluding motor abnormalities. Hierarchical clustering combined normalized sural and "best" upper-limb (UL) SNAP amplitudes with binary indicators for absent responses. Classes were ordered by an NCS severity index and validated against clinical scales. Among 15,744 consecutive examinations, 308 met inclusion criteria. Three well-separated NCS severity classes emerged: mild (reduced but present sural and present UL SNAPs), moderate (absent sural, present UL SNAPs), and severe (absent sural and UL SNAPs). Clinical severity increased monotonically across classes. Patients in the severe class had younger age at symptom onset than those in mild-moderate classes and were more disabled (modified Rankin scale ≥ 2: 50.0% in severe vs 30.4% in moderate vs 16.2% in mild). The severe class was enriched in immune/paraneoplastic (12.5%) and genetic (40.6%) causes. By stratifying patients based on SNAP amplitudes, we identified a differential etiologic enrichment rather than a continuum of disease progression. Severe electrophysiology with motor sparing should prompt RFC1 testing and immune/paraneoplastic work-up, whereas mild to moderate abnormalities should lead to assessment for diabetes and toxic or nutritional exposures.

title: Exome Sequencing Identifies Population-Specific Genetic Risk Factors for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy in Asia.
journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
abstract: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) is a debilitating primary tauopathy. Although genome-wide association studies have identified risk loci in European populations, the genetic architecture of PSP in Asia remains largely undefined. We aimed to identify population-specific genetic risk factors in Asian patients with PSP. We performed whole-exome sequencing in 549 patients with PSP recruited across East and Southeast Asia. Variant frequencies were compared with 1492 whole-genome-sequenced controls from the Taiwan Biobank. Novel variants were functionally evaluated using cellular and Drosophila models. Among 549 patients (mean age at onset 65.1 ± 7.4 years; 60.47% male), 29 (5.28%) carried heterozygous pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants, including 12 novel variants. Additionally, 127 patients (23.13%) harbored 144 rare variants of uncertain significance with minor allele frequency < 1%. Pathogenic variants were most frequently identified in ABCA7 (n = 6, 20.69%) and SMPD1 (n = 6, 20.69%), followed by BSN (n = 3, 10.34%) and MAPT (n = 2, 6.90%). Rare variant landscape analysis identified BSN as the most prominent contributor (38/173 total rare variants, 21.97%), followed by ABCA7 (13.29%), LRRK2 (10.40%), and MAPT (6.94%). Functional studies demonstrated that BSN variants enhance tau aggregation and neurodegeneration. Additionally, the common Asian LRRK2 variants were enriched in PSP, with p.G2385R significantly associated with PSP risk (odds ratio 2.75, 95% CI 1.77-4.32; P < 0.0001) and remained significant compared with Taiwan Biobank controls (P = 0.02), whereas the association for p.R1628P was attenuated. Our findings delineate an ancestry-specific genetic architecture of PSP distinct from the MAPT-dominant pattern observed in European populations, providing mechanistic insights into disease biology. © 2026 International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

title: Triple-signal-amplified competitive immunoassay based on bifunctional multivalent nanobody for high-sensitivity detection of ochratoxin a in coffee.
abstract: Ochratoxin A (OTA) is a widespread toxic mycotoxin that easily accumulates in coffee raw materials and endangers human physical health, which creates an urgent demand for high-sensitivity testing technology suitable for trace toxin detection. Here, we constructed a competitive enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay equipped with three-stage signal amplification (named TA-ELISA) to remarkably improve the overall detection capacity for trace OTA residues. The first amplification module relies on self-assembled heptameric bifunctional nanobody (Nb28-C4-SBP), which effectively elevates antigen binding avidity through multivalent cross-linking. The second amplification unit adopts tyramine signal amplification (TSA) technology, which catalyzes massive deposition of biotin-tyramine conjugates to generate abundant streptavidin binding sites on the solid phase carrier. The final amplification step uses streptavidin-polymerized horseradish peroxidase (SA-PolyHRP) as signal reporter, which carries dozens of HRP catalytic molecules to further amplify colorimetric readout signals. Under fully optimized reaction parameters, the TA-ELISA system achieves a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.012 ng/mL, with sensitivity raised by 5.5 times and 4.0 times compared with single-amplification and dual-amplification detection schemes respectively. For coffee samples spiked with OTA standard, the matrix-matched LOD reaches 183.6 ng/kg, which fully meets the official residue limit standards released by Chinese food safety authorities and European Union regulatory commissions. This triple-amplification competitive immunoassay possesses the merits of ultrahigh sensitivity, simple operation steps and short detection cycle for quantitative analysis of OTA in coffee, and the multi-stage amplification framework proposed in this work can be widely extended to lower the detection threshold of various competitive immunoassay platforms.

title: Antifouling superhydrophilic hydrogel-based electrochemical sensor for robust multi-analyte sweat analysis.
abstract: Reliable sweat analysis in complex biological environments remains challenging due to biofouling-induced signal degradation and analyte interference. Herein, a superhydrophilic antifouling hydrogel-based electrochemical sensor is developed by integrating TiO2-decorated MXene (MXene@TiO2) into a borax-crosslinked PVA network for intelligent multi-analyte sweat analysis. The MXene@TiO2 not only provides conductivity and electrocatalytic activity, but also enhances hydrophilicity of the sensing interface, thereby suppressing nonspecific protein adsorption. The sensor enables sensitive and selective detection of dopamine, uric acid, and ascorbic acid, with detection limits as low as 0.0491, 0.1187, and 0.2451 μM, respectively. Under protein-interference conditions containing 10 mg mL-1 bovine serum albumin (BSA), the current attenuation for DA, UA, and AA was limited to 24.88%, 13.37%, and 12.65%, respectively, demonstrating resistance to biofouling-induced signal loss. Machine-learning-based classification and regression were further employed for analyte identification and concentration prediction, achieving a classification accuracy of 97.9% and an R2 of 0.978 for concentration prediction. Furthermore, a wearable sensing platform incorporating wireless communication and mobile-based data processing enables wearable signal acquisition and intelligent analysis, while droplet-based validation yielded recoveries from 99.45% to 100.80%. By integrating superhydrophilic antifouling interface engineering with machine-learning-assisted signal interpretation, this work provides a robust strategy for intelligent multi-analyte sweat sensing and wearable health monitoring.

title: Dendrobium officinale-derived extracellular vesicles alleviate inflammatory activation in macrophages and modulate NF-κB signaling.
abstract: Macrophage-mediated inflammation responses play a critical role in the progression of inflammatory diseases. In this study, extracellular vesicles derived from Dendrobium officinale (DOEVs) were successfully isolated and characterized, and their physicochemical properties, stability, and anti-inflammatory activities were systematically investigated. DOEVs significantly inhibited nitric oxide production and reduced the expression and secretion of pro-inflammatory mediators, without affecting cell viability. Flow cytometric analysis demonstrated that DOEVs suppressed M1 macrophage polarization. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that DOEVs modulated multiple inflammation-related genes and signaling pathways. Furthermore, DOEVs inhibited NF-κB activation by preventing IκB-α degradation and suppressing p65 nuclear translocation. Collectively, these findings indicate that DOEVs exert anti-inflammatory effects by attenuating macrophage inflammatory activation and modulating NF-κB signaling. This study provides new insights into the biological functions of DOEVs and lays a foundation for future studies exploring their potential nutritional and biomedical applications.

title: Suitability and quality of tencha produced from seven tea cultivars in Guizhou assessed using metabolomics and electronic sensory evaluation.
abstract: This study compared tencha produced from seven tea cultivars grown under the same conditions in Tongren, Guizhou. The cultivars were 'Fuding Dabai' (FDDB), 'Zhongcha 108' (ZC108), 'Mingshan 131' (MS131), 'Baiye No. 1' (BY1H), 'Fuxuan No. 9' (FX9H), 'Guizhou Tea Variety-X' (GZTV-X), and 'Xiapu Chunbolv' (XPCBL). Quality was evaluated by sensory assessment, electronic nose and tongue measurements, HPLC quantification of major taste compounds, and UPLC-MS/MS and gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) metabolite profiling. The cultivars differed in sensory quality and chemical composition. FDDB had the highest overall sensory score (91.85) and the most balanced profile, with high theanine (23.42 mg/g), moderate caffeine, a high non-ester/ester catechin ratio, and comparatively high levels of several floral and fresh-aroma compounds. BY1H ranked second overall and had the strongest aroma response and the lowest caffeine content (22.8 mg/g), although its taste harmony was lower than that of FDDB. GZTV-X had the highest caffeine content (49.91 mg/g), EGCG content, and total catechin content, together with pronounced bitterness and the lowest overall sensory score. MS131 was distinguished by high β-ionone content but had an intermediate overall score. ZC108 was limited mainly by weak aroma, FX9H by poor appearance and high bitterness, and XPCBL by weak aroma together with elevated bitterness and astringency. Under the conditions tested, FDDB was the strongest candidate for further validation in Tongren tencha production. The results show that cultivar suitability is better assessed from combined sensory and chemical evidence than from any single quality indicator.

title: Dynamics of biogenic amine formation in fermented mandarin fish: Insights from precursor utilization and microbial succession.
abstract: The high protein content of mandarin fish (Siniperca chuatsi) provides abundant substrates for biogenic amines (BAs) formation during fermentation, but the temporal dynamics and microbial drivers of BAs accumulation remain unclear. This study systematically investigated the succession of free amino acids (FAAs), BAs, and bacterial communities during fermentation. Results showed that the total FAAs peaked on day 5, whereas total BAs reached a maximum on day 10 (767.58 mg/kg). The BAs surge initiated at day 7.5, approximately 2.5 days after the FAAs peak. Putrescine, cadaverine, histamine, and tyramine were the predominant BAs, accounting for >98% of total BAs. Correlation analysis revealed strong negative correlations between BAs and their precursor FAAs (|R| = 0.588-0.842), suggesting the decarboxylation-driven conversion. Microbial succession identified candidate genera positively associated with BAs accumulation, including Vibrio and Morganella, while the late-stage decline of Vibrio and the increase of Vagococcus coincided with BAs reduction. Metagenomic analysis revealed that amino acid decarboxylase gene abundance peaked at day 10, while BA-degrading gene abundance peaked at day 15, consistent with the BAs dynamics. Days 5 to 10 are identified as a period that may warrant enhanced monitoring in industrial practice. A sequential temporal pattern linking substrate availability, microbial shifts, and BAs dynamics is described. These findings provide insights into the sequential dynamics of BAs formation in fermented mandarin fish and provide a scientific foundation for quality management in traditional fermented fish products.

title: First Opioid Exposure During Adolescent Third Molar Surgery: A Neurodevelopmental Perspective on Opioid Stewardship.
journal: Journal of oral and maxillofacial surgery : official journal of the American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons
abstract: Third molar extraction is commonly performed in adolescents and young adults and may represent an early exposure to prescription opioids. Observational studies have examined whether perioperative opioid prescribing in dentoalveolar surgery is associated with subsequent opioid use. This perspective evaluates epidemiologic findings regarding persistent opioid use after third molar extraction and considers relevant aspects of adolescent neurodevelopment. Retrospective cohort studies report increased adjusted odds of persistent opioid use among some opioid-naive adolescents receiving perioperative dental opioid prescriptions, although absolute risk remains low. Developmental neuroscience demonstrates continued maturation of prefrontal cortical networks during adolescence and heightened reward responsivity, providing biologic context for reinforcement sensitivity. Current evidence does not establish a causal relationship between short-course postoperative opioid prescribing and addiction. However, epidemiologic associations and developmental considerations support continued emphasis on multimodal, opioid-sparing analgesia in adolescent third molar surgery.

title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Molecular Hybrids Incorporating Coumarin-Pyrazole-Linked Indolinone Derivatives With Antioxidant and Anti-Alzheimer Properties.
abstract: The increase in global life expectancy has resulted in a significant rise in the occurrence of Alzheimer's disease (AD), making it a critical public health burden. Therefore, there is an urgent need to create effective methods to prevent or slow down the progression of the disease. In this regard, fifteen previously reported hybrid molecules (7a-c, 10a-j, and 13a,b), combining 4-hydroxycoumarin and pyrazolyl indolin-2-one structures, were resynthesized and tested for their antioxidant and anti-Alzheimer properties. Several of these compounds showed moderate to strong biological activity. Among these, compound 7a demonstrated excellent antioxidant capacity (TAC = 80.65 mg gallic acid/g; IRP = 68.90 µg/mL) and impressive free radical scavenging abilities (DPPH = 5.33 µg/mL; ABTS = 4.59 µg/mL; NO = 6.76 µg/mL), comparable to the standard antioxidant ascorbic acid. Additionally, compound 7a demonstrated the robust inhibition of acetylcholinesterase (AChE) with an IC50 of 6.89 µg/mL, as well as potent inhibition of butyrylcholinesterase (BChE) (IC50 = 5.93 µg/mL). Molecular docking analyses of compound 7a revealed favorable binding interactions and stable conformations within the enzyme's active site, supporting its strong inhibitory effect. Overall, these findings indicate that this group of hybrid molecules offers a promising framework for developing new cholinesterase-targeting treatments for AD.

title: Long-Term Post-Mitotic Culture of Human Fibroblasts Recapitulates and Accelerates Features of In Vivo Aging and Enables Dynamic Testing of Anti-Aging Compounds.
abstract: Biological aging drives cellular dysfunction and human disease, yet studying human aging dynamics remains challenging due to limited experimental platforms. Here we show that long-term post-mitotic culture of human fibroblasts recapitulates and accelerates features of in vivo aging. Longitudinal paired transcriptomic and epigenetic analyses of four female fibroblast lines revealed that in vitro aging reflects key signatures of in vivo primary fibroblast aging. Direct neuronal conversion of in vitro-aged fibroblasts preserved biological age, enabling pseudo-longitudinal modeling of neuronal aging through direct reprogramming. Single-cell transcriptomics of in vitro-aging fibroblasts revealed a time-dependent increase in age-heterogeneity, consistent with the previously reported age-associated heterogeneity driven by the variable loss of transcriptional programs in vivo. Using this accelerated aging platform, we evaluated anti-aging compounds: Metformin broadly attenuated transcriptomic and epigenetic aging, while Rapamycin showed limited efficacy. These findings align with pre-clinical evidence, providing a platform to evaluate and predict therapeutic anti-aging compound efficacy at molecular resolution. This system advances our understanding of aging mechanisms and facilitates the development of interventions against age-related diseases.

title: Chronic kidney disease and blood-based biomarkers of Alzheimer's disease: the brain in kidney disease study.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: Reduced kidney function affects the levels of many Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD) blood-based biomarkers (BBMs). The extent to which kidney function is associated with serum levels of brain-derived tau (BD-tau), a novel BBM specific for Alzheimer's disease-type neurodegeneration, is unknown. ADRD BBMs were measured in stored serum samples from 443 BRain IN Kidney Disease study participants (mean age 68.9 years, 49% female). Lower estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR; poorer kidney function) was inversely associated with levels of serum BD-tau: BD-tau 54.6 pg/mL (standard deviation [SD] 24.47) for eGFR 300 mg/g, 22.57 [21.59] for UACR 30 to 300, and 14 [10.72] for UACR < 30. These trends were consistent for all levels of cognitive impairment (CI; from no CI to severe CI) and persisted following adjustment for age, race, sex, and education. In contrast, associations of kidney function with the pTau217/BD-tau ratio were generally non-significant. Kidney function needs to be considered when interpreting BD-tau levels.

title: Treatment plan quality comparison between ZAP-Axon® Krylov optimizer and Leksell Gamma Knife® Lightning optimizer for brain metastasis.
journal: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
abstract: This study compares stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) treatment plan quality between the recently launched ZAP-Axon® Krylov optimizer and the Leksell Gamma Knife® (LGK) Lightning optimizer for brain metastasis (BM). Thirty (n = 30) patients who were previously treated with LGK SRS or fractionated SRS were selected and divided into three groups: large post-operative resection cavities of BM (BMlg, postop), large intact BM (BMlg, intact) and small intact BM (BMsm, intact). Based on our institutional planning guidelines, the 30 clinical cases were replanned using ZAP-Axon Krylov and LGK Lightning optimizers without manual adjustments. Statistical analysis was performed to compare plan quality metrics (Paddick conformity index [PCI], gradient index [GI], target coverage [TC], prescribed isodose line [Rx IDL], and treatment time/scaled beam-on-time [sBOT] [min]) between the two optimizers. For the BMlg, postop group, mean values of PCI, GI, TC, Rx IDL, and treatment time/sBOT (min) for Krylov versus Lightning plans were 0.91 versus 0.91, 2.48 versus 2.56, 99.5% versus 99.7%, 51.1% versus 53.7% and 37.4 min versus 36.5 min, respectively. All metrics except for the Rx IDL (%) were not statistically significantly different. For the BMlg, intact group, corresponding values were 0.93 versus 0.93, 2.42 versus 2.57, 99.5% versus 99.7%. 51.5% versus 53.0% and 35.9 min versus 36.3 min. While GI was statistically significantly different (p <0.05) between the two optimizers, the rest of the metrics were not. For the BMsm, intact group, corresponding values were 0.71 versus 0.64, 3.10 versus 3.26, 99.5% versus 99.5%, 61.9% versus 53.0% and 8.1 min versus 19.8 min. In this group, PCI and treatment time/sBOT were statistically significantly different (p <0.05), whereas GI and Rx IDL were not. Without manual adjustments, ZAP-Axon Krylov plans were comparable to LGK Lightning plans for large BM lesions, but the Krylov optimizer outperformed the Lightning optimizer for small BM lesions.

title: Hesperidin from Citrus reticulata peel improves welfare in PTU-induced hypothyroid rats through home-cage behavioral, endocrine, neurobehavioral, and anti-inflammatory mechanisms.
abstract: Hesperidin, a major flavanone glycoside of Citrus reticulata peel, possesses antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, its therapeutic effects on hypothyroidism-associated inflammatory, neurobehavioral, and welfare disturbances remain insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated the efficacy of hesperidin versus levothyroxine in a propylthiouracil (PTU)-induced hypothyroid rat model, with particular emphasis on continuous home-cage behavioral monitoring as a non-invasive indicator of welfare impairment and therapeutic recovery. Thirty-five adult female Sprague Dawley rats were allocated to control, hypothyroid, levothyroxine-treated, and low- and high-dose hesperidin-treated groups. Endocrine, growth, behavioral, oxidative, inflammatory, apoptotic, and histopathological parameters were assessed. PTU-induced hypothyroidism was characterized by reduced T3 and T4, elevated TSH, impaired growth and home-cage behavior, cognitive deficits, increased TNF-α, IL-1β, and caspase-3 expression, and marked tissue lesions. Hesperidin markedly ameliorated these alterations, with the high dose producing pronounced improvements in endocrine homeostasis, welfare-related behavior, oxidative stress, inflammatory and apoptotic responses, and tissue architecture. These findings demonstrate the multitarget therapeutic potential of hesperidin in PTU-induced hypothyroidism and support its potential as an adjunctive approach for alleviating endocrine dysfunction and associated welfare impairment.

title: Psychiatry of ophthalmology: Proposing the ophthalmo-psychiatric disorders framework.
abstract: We propose the ophthalmo-psychiatric disorders (OPD) framework as an organizing clinical and research model at the interface of vision science and mental health, and to synthesize, with wording calibrated to evidence strength, bidirectional relationships between ophthalmic disease, visual function, and psychiatric states. Visual impairment and common mental disorders co-distribute globally, with adults with vision loss showing roughly two-to three-fold higher prevalence of depressive and anxiety symptoms than visually normal peers. Elevated psychiatric comorbidity across glaucoma, dry eye disease, and age-related macular degeneration is supported by systematic reviews and meta-analyses, as is the benefit of psychological and stepped-care intervention. Mechanistic claims are weaker: hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal and autonomic dysregulation, inflammation, circadian disruption, central sensitization, and retinal neurodegeneration remain candidate pathways resting largely on cross-sectional data, and retinal findings in severe mental illness are group-level associations confounded by lifestyle, metabolic, medication, and imaging factors. The eye and the mind are anatomically and physiologically connected. The concept of OPD provides a pragmatic biopsychosocial framework that moves beyond an "organic versus non-organic (functional)" dichotomy and highlights the clinical intersection of the 2 fields. Progress will depend on interdisciplinary training, longitudinal research with harmonized definitions, and culturally sensitive implementation of eye-mind care.

title: Modeling the Action-Perception loop and its role in phantom limb pain using active inference.
abstract: Mathematical models grounded in the Bayesian inference framework have been used to describe various aspects of pain perception. However, pain is not only passively inferred but actively shaped through interactions with the environment - a dimension that classical Bayesian approaches typically do not capture. Here, we investigate the role of the action-perception loop in phantom limb pain using a model within the active inference framework, which extends Bayesian inference to include action selection. Despite being one of the most prevalent and distressing consequences of limb amputation, theories regarding the underlying mechanisms of phantom limb pain remain disputed. Because amputation disrupts both sensory input related to the limb and the ability to perform actions, a model incorporating both sensory and active components of pain may provide new mechanistic insight into this condition. The presented model provides a conceptual account of how loss of limb control, ambiguity in sensory input pertaining to limb position, residual noxious input, and pre-amputation pain may contribute to the emergence and persistence of phantom limb pain. Furthermore, the model offers insight into the possible mechanisms underlying common interventions and may help account for their variable efficacy across individuals.

title: Contralateral Seventh Cervical Nerve Transfer Drives Staged Central Remodeling After Traumatic Brain Injury: A Multiscale Resting-State fMRI Study.
abstract: Contralateral seventh cervical nerve transfer (CC7) improves paretic-limb function after unilateral brain injury, but how peripheral rerouting reshapes distributed brain systems remain unclear. Here, we used longitudinal resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging in a mouse traumatic brain injury model to determine whether CC7 is associated with multiscale reorganization of intrinsic brain function. Across post-transfer stages, functional connectivity density showed distinct stage-related spatial patterns, with predominantly contralesional sensorimotor involvement at earlier follow-up stages and additional striatal and hippocampal involvement at later stages, whereas regional homogeneity and fractional amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations showed complementary changes in local coordination and regional activity involving limbic-parahippocampal, thalamic, and sensorimotor regions. CC7 also improved late-phase skilled grasping, and secondary motor cortex and CA1 hubness correlated positively with behavioral recovery. These findings suggest that CC7-related recovery is not limited to contralesional sensorimotor compensation but increasingly recruits higher-order motor and learning-related systems, supporting a model of staged adaptive central remodeling after brain injury.

title: Bioelectrical and optogenetic modulation for neuroimmune therapeutics.
abstract: Neuroimmune interactions are emerging as key regulators of inflammation, immunity, immune homeostasis, and disease progression. Neural circuits do not merely sense tissue injury, but also actively shape immune-cell recruitment, cytokine production, vascular function, and organ-level inflammatory outcomes. Here, we overview bioelectrical and optogenetic systems for neuroimmune modulation in diseases via the defined neural and inflammatory pathway. First, we review systemic neuroimmune modulating pathway and local neuroimmune modulators, and identify established neuroimmune molecular interactions in diseases. After that, we explain bioelectrical and optogenetic systems employed to modulate neuroimmune interactions. We evaluate representative studies with advanced delivery systems in consideration of neural target, immune effector, disease-relevant outcome, and safety. Finally, this review highlights both positive and negative clinical evidence of electroceuticals, and ultrasound-mediated and optogenetic systems predominantly in preclinical development. In summary and perspective, we prioritize and discuss the requirements for their further clinical translation. The integration of neural targeting with advanced materials and adaptive gene and drug delivery would be successfully harnessed for programmable therapies to modulate disease-relevant immune circuits without broadly suppressing host defense systems.

title: Establishing a Biophotonic Signature of Brain Ageing.
abstract: Ageing-associated inflammation ("inflammaging") is characterised by chronic microglial priming or overactivity that elevates neurodegeneration risk. Microglia also accumulate autofluorescent lipofuscin as they age-aggregates of oxidised lipids, misfolded proteins and metals that generate reactive oxygen species. Characterising age-related changes in brain autofluorescence could provide insight into brain ageing dynamics and could identify associations with potential biomarkers in accessible tissues such as blood. We hypothesised that the ageing-related increase in microglial autofluorescent material produces a spectral signature that makes ageing autofluorescence distinct from that in young brains. To test this, we examined autofluorescence profiles in the hippocampus and arcuate nucleus (ARC) of young (3 months) and aged (21 months) female C57BL/6 mice. We found that ageing significantly increased the volume of the autofluorescent material in microglia, including driving an abundance of extra-large aggregates. In the ARC, larger aggregates-present only in aged brains-exhibited stronger far-red emission than the autofluorescence seen in young brains. Fluorescence lifetime imaging analysis indicated specific ageing-related molecular changes in brain autofluorescence. Lipidomic analysis from the plasma of these mice indicated 22 lipids that were differentially concentrated with age and one (sphingomyelin 32:2) that was significantly associated with the ageing brain spectral profile after controlling for multiple comparisons and validating in a separate cohort. These findings demonstrate that autofluorescent material aggregates with age in microglia and that brain autofluorescence undergoes a spectral red-shift associated with ageing and lipid alterations. Brain autofluorescence may thus reflect brain ageing with potential translational relevance for non-invasive monitoring.

title: UHRF proteins as epigenetic integrators coordinating DNA methylation, histone modifications, and chromatin remodeling.
abstract: UHRF1 and UHRF2 are multidomain epigenetic regulators that are paralogous in structure but slightly different in function. UHRF1 main function is to participate in replication coupled maintenance DNA methylation. UHRF1 recognizes hemi-methylated DNA and specific histone states, and it recruits and activates DNMT1 to newly replicated chromatin. This function is a key mechanism for faithful DNA methylation transmission and maintenance of cellular identity. In various cancers, abnormal UHRF1 activity has been linked to abnormal chromatin regulation, genome instability, tumour progression, and resistance to therapy.
