UHRF2 preferentially binds 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), a cytosine modification that is particularly enriched in brain tissue and in differentiated post-mitotic cells. Through this recognition, UHRF2 engages chromatin and DNA repair factors, including XRCC1, linking 5hmC to both chromatin regulation and repair at hydroxymethylated sites. While the UHRF2-5hmC-XRCC1 axis is supported by direct biochemical evidence, its broader roles in neuronal regulation, memory, and development mainly on genetic models and context-dependent observations. Both proteins undergo post-translational modifications, including phosphorylation, ubiquitination, acetylation, and SUMOylation, which affect protein stability, localization, chromatin binding, and molecular activity. This review examines the domain architecture, DNA and histone recognition mechanisms, cell cycle regulation, genome maintenance functions, disease associations, and therapeutic relevance of UHRF1 and UHRF2. It focuses on the difference between UHRF1 associated epigenetic inheritance and UHRF2 associated hydroxymethylation dependent chromatin plasticity. The review also addresses novel therapeutic approaches such as domain selective inhibition, targeted protein degradation, and distinguishes preclinical results from clinically validated findings. These similarities and differences between the paralogs could help design more selective and biologically relevant epigenetic treatments.

title: Mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes as nanocarriers for curcumin: from fundamental research to clinical translation.
abstract: Curcumin has diverse pharmacological activities but poor water solubility, rapid degradation, extensive metabolism, and very low oral bioavailability limit its therapeutic use. This review evaluates mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (MSC-Exo; MSC-derived small extracellular vesicles per MISEV2023) as natural nanocarriers for curcumin delivery and the barriers to clinical translation. Curcumin-loaded MSC-Exo (Cur@Exos) can improve curcumin stability, sustain release, enhance target-tissue accumulation, and cross biological barriers such as the blood-brain barrier. Compared with synthetic nanocarriers, MSC-Exo may offer better biocompatibility, immune evasion, and tissue tropism, but these properties depend on source and preparation; proteomes, miRNA cargoes, and functions differ among bone marrow-, umbilical cord-, and adipose-derived MSCs. Encapsulation efficiency, batch consistency, scalability, and storage stability also remain suboptimal. Preclinical studies show Cur@Exos benefits in neurodegenerative diseases, rheumatoid arthritis, liver disease, wound healing, bone defects, and sepsis-associated kidney injury. However, findings are limited by heterogeneity in exosome sources, preparation, loading methods, and animal models; small samples and short follow-up; inconsistent dose metrics (particle number vs. protein content); and lack of standardized process and outcome criteria, reference materials, and potency assays. Long-term safety remains inadequately established: current evidence covers only short-term single or repeated dosing; ≥ 6-month repeat-dose toxicology with anti-drug antibody and complement monitoring, predictive immunogenicity screening, tumorigenicity assessment, potency-based batch release testing, and clinical efficacy data are lacking. MSC-Exo is a promising curcumin-delivery platform, but translation requires standardized manufacturing, globally harmonized quality control, improved scalability, systematic safety evaluation, well-designed multicenter trials, and a clarified international regulatory pathway.

title: MyotonPRO-derived hamstring mechanical properties across testing positions and their associations with maximal strength.
abstract: The MyotonPRO is increasingly used to quantify skeletal muscle mechanical properties; however, hamstring measurements may vary across testing positions, and the relationships between these measurements and maximal strength remain unclear. This study investigated differences in MyotonPRO-derived mechanical properties of the biceps femoris and semitendinosus across four testing positions and examined their exploratory associations with maximal isometric hamstring strength. Thirty healthy adults (18 males, 12 females; age 27.4 ± 4.9 years) underwent MyotonPRO assessment in the prone position, prone with the knee flexed to 90°, bilateral standing, and single-leg standing. Oscillation frequency, dynamic stiffness, logarithmic decrement, relaxation time, and creep were measured in both muscles. Maximal isometric hamstring strength was assessed using the End Range Hamstring Strength Test with handheld dynamometry. MyotonPRO-derived mechanical properties differed significantly across testing positions, with large position effects (partial η2 = 0.355-0.822). Stiffness and oscillation frequency generally increased toward weight-bearing positions, whereas relaxation time and creep decreased; logarithmic decrement showed a less consistent pattern. Exploratory correlation analyses showed moderate-to-strong associations between maximal hamstring strength and stiffness, frequency, and relaxation time, as well as creep (|r| = 0.38-0.67), whereas logarithmic decrement showed weaker and more variable associations. In an exploratory hierarchical regression, adding logarithmic decrement to the selected stiffness measure increased R2 from 0.440 to 0.500, but the incremental change was not statistically significant (ΔR2 = 0.060, p = 0.082). These findings indicate that MyotonPRO-derived hamstring mechanical properties differ across testing positions and should therefore be interpreted within standardized testing conditions.

title: CT-based adaptation of the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score in advanced ovarian cancer: Agreement and inter-reader reproducibility.
abstract: To evaluate agreement of proposed CT-based variants with the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score in suspected advanced ovarian cancer and assess inter-reader agreement of CT-derived components. This retrospective single-center study included consecutive adults evaluated between January 2021 and November 2025 for suspected advanced ovarian cancer who underwent contrast-enhanced abdominopelvic CT and staging laparoscopy. Proposed CT-based modifications were operationalized as six score variants combining CT-derived peritoneal tumor burden, CT-estimated ascites, cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), and either Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG-PS) or CT-derived body composition parameters. Agreement with the laparoscopic risk-adjusted score was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Spearman correlation coefficient, and weighted Cohen's kappa. The final cohort included 80 patients. All CT-based variants showed agreement with the laparoscopic risk-adjusted score. For the variant combining CT-derived PCI, CT-estimated ascites, ECOG-PS, and CA-125, the consistency ICC was 0.76, Spearman's ρ was 0.806, and weighted Cohen's kappa was 0.76. This variant showed 70.0% agreement across the three risk categories and 83.8% agreement for high-risk versus non-high-risk classification, classifying 20 of 22 laparoscopic high-risk patients as high risk. The PCI-based skeletal muscle index (SMI) variant maintained substantial agreement: ICC, 0.73; Spearman correlation coefficient, 0.742; weighted Cohen's kappa, 0.74. Inter-reader agreement was high for CT-derived PCI, with an ICC of 0.91. Proposed CT-based variants showed agreement with the Vizzielli laparoscopic risk-adjusted score. The PCI-based ECOG-PS variant showed the highest agreement metrics, suggesting that structured CT assessment may help approximate laparoscopic risk categories before invasive evaluation.

title: The innovator's mind in neurosurgery: psychological traits and historical lessons from neurosurgical device development and adoption.
AAV-BDNF modulates 5HT2A receptor, glycine receptor subunits, and Nav1.1 channel gene expression in lumbar motoneurons after spinal cord injury.
abstract: Proper excitability of spinal motor neurons (MNs) is essential for motor output. Spinal cord injury (SCI) disrupts this network and compromises MN- driven skeletal muscle contractions. We previously showed that tracer-identified MNs innervating ankle extensor and flexor muscles display gene-expression changes toward a more excitatory profile at 2 weeks post-lesion in rats, however, this shift does not restore stepping. Given evidence that brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) enhances MN excitability and promotes functional recovery, we investigated its effects on gene expression following SCI. Adult male rats received retrograde tracers in gastrocnemius lateralis (GL) and tibialis anterior (TA) muscles. Two weeks later, complete low-thoracic transection was followed by bilateral lumbar L1-L2 injection of AAV-BDNF or PBS. Locomotion was assessed on a treadmill and in an open field. BDNF and TrkB transcripts were assessed by RNAscope, while selected receptor, transporter, and ion-channel transcripts were measured in lumbar segments and laser-microdissected GL and TA MNs by RT-qPCR. At two weeks, AAV-BDNF increased spinal BDNF transcript levels and restored TrkB transcripts in lumbar MNs. It improved treadmill locomotion with plantar placement, alternating step-like movements, and body-weight support, while open-field hindlimb movements were also improved. BDNF selectively increased Htr2a transcripts, particularly in GL MNs, and reduced glycine receptor subunit transcripts. It also reversed SCT-induced Scn1a upregulation in GL and TA MNs. Changes in glutamatergic and GABAA receptor transcripts were selective and MN-population dependent. These findings show that intraspinal AAV-BDNF is associated with locomotor recovery and transcriptional changes in MN excitability-related genes. The results support a role for BDNF in spinal circuit reactivation after SCT.

title: Targeting RIPK1-NF-κB crosstalk: A novel perspective on necroptosis in Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative condition characterised by gradual neuronal degradation, resulting in cognitive decline and memory loss. Multiple pathogenic mechanisms drive the progression of the disease, including amyloid-β (Aβ) and tau accumulation (neurofibrillary tangles), mitochondrial dysfunction, synaptic loss, chronic neuroinflammation, and neuro​nal death. Neuronal loss in AD occurs through various forms of regulated cell death, including apoptosis, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, parthanatos, and necroptosis, each characterised by specific pathways and subsequent inflammatory consequences. Despite decades of focus on apoptosis and necrosis as the primary modes of neuronal loss, necroptosis has remained relatively understudied until recently. Necroptosis is a caspase-independent, inflammatory cell death pathway governed by the RIPK1-RIPK3-MLKL signalling axis. Activation of this pathway disrupts plasma membrane integrity, triggering the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) that sustain a self-propagating cycle of neuroinflammation and secondary neuronal loss. Crucially, RIPK1 signalling is closely linked to nuclear factor-[Formula: see text]B (NF-[Formula: see text]B), a principal modulator of inflammatory and cell-survival mechanisms. Although NF-[Formula: see text]B activation can facilitate neuronal survival under physiological conditions, its sustained activation in the AD brain promotes the synthesis of pro-inflammatory mediators, thereby accelerating neurodegeneration. This review discusses the emerging role of RIPK1-mediated necroptosis in AD and examines its functional interaction with NF-[Formula: see text]B signalling in driving neuroinflammation. Additionally, it examines emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the RIPK1-NF-[Formula: see text]B axis to alter disease progression and achieve disease-modifying potential in AD.

title: Membrane-Targeted Nanoparticles for Neuronal Photomodulation.
abstract: Selective targeting of nanoparticles to the neuronal interface is central for the tailored development of precision neurotechnologies. Here, we report the targeting of gold bipyramids, as a model nanomaterial, on the membrane of primary neurons using a bioorthogonal approach. In a two-step process, linker molecules anchor to receptors that expose trans-cyclooctene, which forms a covalent bond with the tetrazine functional group on nanoparticles, leading to the retention of hundreds of nanoparticles per cell. Selective labeling of neuronal membranes with plasmonic nanoparticles via a bioorthogonal strategy enabled inhibition of neuronal activity through photothermal effects under NIR laser irradiation in synchronized cell cultures. The linker and/or nanoparticles alone have a negligible effect on neuromodulation. Nanoparticle retention at the membrane is rapid, requiring only one hour of total incubation, with no cytotoxic effect. These results expand the repertoire of light-activated nanomaterials for non-invasive neuromodulation.

title: Sex Hormones as Regulators of the Age- and Sex-Dependent Benefits of Caloric Restriction: An Emerging Research Protocol of a Controlled Dietary Intervention (The GendAge Weight Loss Study).
abstract: With nearly two-thirds of the UK population living with overweight or obesity, there is an urgent necessity for evidence-based public health guidance to promote a healthy weight. Current weight management advice centres on lifestyle modification. However, existing dieting recommendations fail to consider sex or age. This is a surprising oversight, as it is well established that health outcomes vary significantly between men and women across the lifespan. Our preliminary work in mice and humans suggests young females are more resistant than males to calorie-restriction (CR)-induced fat loss and reductions in energy expenditure, and that this resistance diminishes in older, post-menopausal participants-implicating oestrogen as a possible modulator of CR response. Further, the menopause may have an impact on fat storage linked to changes in sex hormones. This article describes emerging research being done through a controlled feeding study in 75 younger and older men and women. This study will directly test whether CR's effects on fat mass, energy expenditure and glucose homeostasis are age- and sex-dependent, and whether HRT use in post-menopausal women restores a CR response more similar to that of younger women. Energy expenditure and body composition will be assessed using gold-standard techniques, including doubly labelled water, alongside blood and abdominal adipose tissue sampling to investigate underlying hormonal mechanisms. The findings of this new study will clarify whether dietary weight-management advice should be tailored by sex, age, or menopausal/HRT status, informing more precise, evidence-based obesity guidance and supporting women's health and healthy ageing.

title: Performance of the Lausanne Ischemic Stroke Pathway prehospital triage system in identifying acute reperfusion candidates: a quality-control study.
abstract: Accurate identification is one of the cornerstones of prehospital care for patients with suspected acute ischaemic stroke (AIS). In the Lausanne Ischemic Stroke Pathway triage system, emergency medical service (EMS) providers use dedicated criteria to identify acute reperfusion candidates and call a coordinated medical team (CMT, including a neurologist and an emergency physician), which can activate the stroke code pathway. The objective of this study was to evaluate the performance of the system in identifying acute reperfusion candidates. This was a retrospective single-centre quality-control study conducted in a Swiss university-based stroke centre, from 1 January 2019 to 31 May 2022. Inclusion criteria were patients aged ≥18 years, for whom the EMS called the CMT or patients with AIS eligible for acute reperfusion managed by the EMS. The main outcomes were the performance of both the EMS and the CMT in detecting AIS patients eligible for acute reperfusion, as assessed through their respective under- and overtriage rates. A secondary outcome was the identification of alternative diagnoses in overtriaged patients. Of 1071 patients included, the EMS phone-contacted the CMT for 937 (87.5%) of them. Among the 1071 patients, 440 (41%) had an AIS eligible for reperfusion. The system's undertriage rate was 30% (133 patients without stroke pathway activation among the 440 patients with an AIS eligible for acute reperfusion). The undertriage rates were 21% for the EMS and 11% for the CMT. The overtriage rates were 63% for the EMS and 57% for the CMT. The main alternative diagnoses in overtriaged patients were seizures (14%), intracranial haemorrhages (9.9%) and functional disorders (6.5%). Undertriage and overtriage rates were relatively high, but both were reduced by the CMT call, highlighting the added value of a second expert assessment step, with a higher level of expertise. Concerning overtriage, a better prehospital identification of alternative diagnoses, such as seizures or functional disorders, could help to better classify our patients.

title: Evolutionary perspectives on GLP-1 receptor agonists and the modern obesity, sedentary behaviour, and loneliness epidemics.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have transformed obesity and diabetes treatments and show promise for many other health conditions, warranting an examination of their broader health effects. We examine obesity, sedentary behaviour, and loneliness through an evolutionary medicine framework, assessing GLP-1RAs' role in buffering or exacerbating mismatches between novel environments and our evolved physiology. We searched for relevant GLP-1RA papers through PubMed utilising keywords such as "physical activity," "social," and "qualitative," and synthesise important findings in this narrative review. GLP-1RAs buffer against the negative health effects of obesogenic foods through the drugs' effects on our neurobiology. These drugs may mitigate the effects of sedentary lifestyles, as it is easier to exercise without excess weight. However, rapid drug-induced weight loss may reduce fat-free mass if behavioural interventions (e.g. strength training) are not undertaken. Finally, we discuss the mismatch of reduced social eating and associated loneliness. While little data exists on the social effects of GLP-1RAs, emerging evidence suggests that GLP-1RAs may alleviate or intensify loneliness depending on an individual's milieu and specific drug response. Our novel environments increasingly challenge human health. GLP-1RAs may help us manage these mismatches in some ways and exacerbate them in others.

title: Emergence of natalizumab anti-drug antibodies during extended interval dosing in a patient with multiple sclerosis: A case report.
authors: van den Berg Stefan P H
abstract: We present a natalizumab-treated patient with multiple sclerosis (MS) who developed neutralizing anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) after years of treatment following introduction of extended interval dosing (EID). To gain insight into how this sudden ADA development occurred. A pharmacokinetic model was used to evaluate the relation between natalizumab concentration and ADA production. EID from 4 to 6 weeks resulted in unexpectedly low natalizumab trough concentrations accompanied by increasing ADAs. Modeling suggested ADA production was stimulated by declining natalizumab concentrations. EID may result in increased ADA production, causing ADA-mediated clearance of natalizumab and risking new MS activity.

title: Hepatic Stellate Cells: Fibrogenic Effectors to Central Regulators of Metabolism, Liver Disease Signaling, and Systemic Crosstalk.
abstract: Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) have long been regarded as the core effector cells in liver fibrosis. The advent of single-cell omics and metabolomics has led to a paradigm shift in our understanding of these cells. Notably, they are not only implicated in local fibrosis but are being increasingly recognized as a hub integrating metabolic and immune signaling. Located at the interface between hepatic vasculature and parenchyma, HSCs have the capacity to modulate intestinal barrier function, neurotransmitter circulation, myocardial energy metabolism, and bone remodeling through metabolic reprogramming (enhanced glycolysis, vitamin A consumption, glutamine metabolism remodeling) and receptor signaling (TLR4, TGF-β, CXCR4, etc.), as well as by secreting metabolites, exosomal miRNAs, and cytokines. Concurrently, HSCs perceive feedback signals from these organs, forming a dynamic cross-organ feedback network. This review systematically integrates the metabolic characteristics of HSCs in diseases such as metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, chronic viral hepatitis, and hepatocellular carcinoma, along with their cross-organ interactive effects. We further discuss intervention strategies targeting metabolic pathways, exosomal cargo, and the microbiota-metabolism axis, and propose a three-tier translational framework stratifying HSC-targeted therapeutic approaches by developmental stage, offering novel insights for shifting liver disease treatment from single antifibrotic approaches toward systemic, multi-organ precision interventions.

title: The role of microglia in remyelination: Mechanisms and therapeutic implications in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic demyelinating disease of the central nervous system, accompanied by progressive neurological deficits. Current MS disease-modifying drugs mainly target peripheral immune cells and have demonstrated little efficacy for neuroprotection or remyelination. Growing evidence indicates that microglia play a critical dual role in demyelinating animal models and MS. In acute inflammatory phases, microglia adopt a pro-inflammatory phenotype, exacerbating demyelination and neural damage. But, as lesions evolve, these resident immune cells can transform into an anti-inflammatory state, promoting tissue repair and myelin regeneration. Despite the importance of microglia, the regulatory mechanism of this double-edged sword during demyelination and remyelination has not been fully elucidated. This review first provides an overview of the involvement of microglia in demyelination and remyelination, and how their functional evolution depends on disease stage, on the spatial location of the lesion and its microenvironment. Secondly, the interaction between microglia and astrocytes, monocyte-derived macrophages, T cells, and B cells is described, working together to balance the disrupted microenvironment, promote the formation, differentiation, and maturation of oligodendrocyte precursor cells, and ultimately achieve myelin protection and regeneration. We then organize the signaling pathways targeting microglia and remyelination, providing a theoretical basis for drug development. Finally, we present drugs or small-molecule compounds targeting signaling pathways for exploratory therapeutic research at different stages. In summary, this review highlights the importance of remyelination, microglial heterogeneity, the temporal nature of regulation, and the complexity of treatment. We also present some challenges and solutions for remyelination, providing valuable information for neurological recovery in MS patients.

title: Treatment Adherence and its Association with Demographic Characteristics and Clinical Factors Among Patients with Hypertension: A Cross-Sectional, Descriptive-Correlational Study.
abstract: A blood pressure of 140/90 and above indicates high blood pressure. High blood pressure, a silent killer, is a major public health problem. Research has shown that treatment adherence plays an important role in controlling hypertension. Therefore, this study aimed to determine the level of treatment adherence among patients with high blood pressure in the health center of Semnan, 2024. In this cross-sectional study, 400 patients with high blood pressure in the health center of Semnan were selected using a multistage sampling method and enrolled after meeting the inclusion and exclusion criteria. After obtaining informed consent, demographic information and treatment adherence questionnaires were completed. Of the patients, 54.3% were female. The mean ± standard deviation of age was 48.2 ± 18.2 years, with a median of 49 years. The mean ± standard deviation of the treatment adherence score was 83.8 ± 12.4 (out of 115), with a median of 89.6. Overall, 77.5% (95%CI: 73.4%-81.6%) of the patients were adherent to treatment (score ≥86). Treatment adherence was not significantly associated with age, gender, body mass index, marital status, educational level, employment status, number of children, income level, medical history, blood pressure, medication-related variables, duration of hypertension, duration of antihypertensive treatment, or other comorbidities (p > 0.05). Most patients had high treatment adherence, and no demographic characteristics were significantly associated with treatment adherence. Evidence indicates that knowledge influences patients' health behaviors. Therefore, policymakers and healthcare planners should prioritize educating patients with hypertension about the importance of lifestyle modification for the prevention, management, and control of hypertension. The study has several limitations, including reliance on self-reported data, its cross-sectional design, and limited generalizability of the findings.

title: Patient-centred workload clustering in adults under 65 with long-term conditions from longitudinal primary care data.
abstract: Although patient workload is increasingly recognised as a relevant dimension of the patient experience, it is not satisfactorily captured in current electronic health records. We set out to describe the distribution of patient workload patterns across long-term conditions and demographic groups using electronic health records annotated to reflect patient-centred workload derived from a qualitative evidence synthesis of patient experience. We used a predefined compendium of 63 workload indicators, derived from a previously published qualitative evidence synthesis of patient experience and mapped to electronic health record codes, classified into eight themes. We computed counts of these indicators in 765 930 patients born between 1956 and 1965 with two or more recorded long-term conditions, randomly sampled from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink. We then used an unsupervised learning approach to construct a typology of patients based on these counts. Median age at first record was 31 years with 28 years of follow-up. The cohort was 49.4% (n=378 154) male and predominantly white (68.1%, n=521 859). Patients had a median of 15 workload indicators and 4 long-term conditions. Nine clusters were identified, with marked contrasts in workload intensity, long-term conditions, demographic profiles and size. While large clusters were less burdensome, smaller clusters showed more complex profiles, characterised by cardiometabolic or mental health long-term conditions, higher female-to-male ratios and greater ethnic diversity. The most burdensome cluster, characterised by a broad spectrum of rarer long-term conditions and dominated by indicators associated with investigation and treatment monitoring, appeared comparatively less complex. This unsupervised approach to patient workload revealed patient clusters with marked disparities in burden, long-term conditions, demographic characteristics and complexity, supporting future research directions aimed at better understanding and supporting patients with elevated workload demands.

title: The Golden Neuroplastic Period: A Framework for Standardised Patient-centred Stroke Rehabilitation.
abstract: The issue of stroke continues to pose a serious problem for the world community with forecasts of a 50% increase in stroke-associated mortality rate by 2050. Around 90% of patients who suffered from stroke have cognitive deficits. Post-stroke recovery is the fastest within three months, and an interdisciplinary approach including cognitive, nutrition and motor rehabilitation can significantly improve patients' quality of life. The current review highlights the latest advances in interdisciplinary stroke rehabilitation and reveals the key components which are required for precision rehabilitation and durable recovery. An electronic database search was done using the following databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar) until March 2026 according to the PRISMA guidelines. Based on screening of 235 studies, there were included 17 articles into the narrative review. For 43,000 stroke patients, interdisciplinary approach to treatment planning was associated with higher survival rate and functional independence compared with conventional care. Timely start of intervention and treatment within 14 days were connected with better motor results, and participation of neuropsychologists in the stroke team increased the cost-benefit ratio three times due to decrease in social care expenses. To move towards evidence-based treatment and precision rehabilitation, it is imperative to identify the 'active ingredients' of therapy: specific doses of exercise, dual-task complexity and specific timing for nutritional supplementation. Standardised and cost-effective models should be widely implemented to decrease the burden of caregivers and support long-term brain health.

title: Value of positive RT-QuIC replicate number in sporadic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.
abstract: Real-time quaking-induced conversion (RT-QuIC) of recombinant prion protein is a biomarker for Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (CJD). RT-QuIC assesses a sample's seeding activity across multiple wells. We aim to model the test within a binomial framework and describe possible applications. This is a single-centre retrospective observational study. CJD and non-CJD cases with cerebrospinal fluid RT-QuIC were enrolled (2014-2018). The probability of a positive event in one well (θ+) for each group was assessed. θ+ can be used to calculate the posterior probability of disease (P_post) or as input parameters for computer simulations. Data from 584 sporadic CJD (sCJD) and 226 non-CJD cases were used. Respectively, θ+ was 0.841 (95% CI 0.823 to 0.857) and 0.025 (95% CI 0.016 to 0.040). The distribution of RT-QuIC results did not differ between all sCJD samples and definite sCJD cases and across groups with different alleles at codon 129 of the PRNP gene. P_post was calculated for each result. The distribution of results did not differ significantly across years in def/prob-sCJD and non-CJD. RT-QuIC results distribution and θ+ may be used for intra-laboratory quality control and P_post determination. Future studies should explore the utility of θ+ to increase diagnostic accuracy and inter-laboratory comparison.

title: Novel Creation of Three-Dimensional Virtual Reality Neuroanatomy Specimens Through Freely-Available Software.
abstract: Conceptualizing the three-dimensional (3D) relationships between different brain structures represents a pervasive challenge for students learning neuroanatomy. Recent technological advances allow for the creation of adaptable, future-ready curricula and enhanced remote learning neuroanatomy resources. Here, we describe methodology for generating a 3D virtual reality brain using freely-available software.

title: Benefits of Integrating Standardized Patient Encounters into Pre-clerkship Neurology Curriculum.
abstract: Standardized patient encounters (SPEs) are a foundational tool in medical education, yet their pre-clerkship role in undergraduate medical education, particularly in neuroscience, remains less clearly defined. This study evaluates the impact of integrating SPEs into a pre-clerkship Nervous System course on student knowledge, diagnostic confidence, and performance. Our objective was to design reproducible neurology-focused SPEs for pre-clerkship learners and assess its effectiveness in improving knowledge acquisition and diagnostic confidence with common neurological conditions. Second-year medical students at our institution who were enrolled in a 6-week Nervous System course participated in four structured SPEs addressing common neurologic presentations. Students conducted focused neurologic histories, examinations, and diagnostic reasoning. Knowledge was assessed using a 10-item quiz administered before and after the SPEs. Performance on 12 SPE-related NBME final exam questions was compared with national averages. Diagnostic confidence was evaluated using pre- and post-SPE self-assessment surveys. Students demonstrated significant improvement in knowledge, with a median quiz score increase of 1.0 point (Hodges-Lehmann estimate, 95% CI: 0.0-3.5; p < 0.0001). On the NBME exam, our students outperformed national averages across nearly all SPE-related items (FIU mean = 0.87 vs. 0.71; p < 0.05). Students also reported significant increases in diagnostic confidence across all neurologic conditions assessed (all p < 0.001). Integration of SPEs into a pre-clerkship neurology course resulted in immediate gains in knowledge and confidence, and higher standardized exam performance, underscoring SPEs as a valuable early experiential learning modality in clinical neuroscience education.

title: Looking Closely at the Human Experience: Visual Art-Based Exercises in Preclinical Neuroscience Education.
abstract: Preclinical neuroscience often feels abstract, contributes to neurophobia, and may obscure the patient experience. Visual arts-based learning may strengthen observation and interpretation. We integrated gamified, visual arts-based exercises into readiness assessment questions in a required six-week preclinical neuroscience course for 172 s-year medical students. All students completed the exercises. Of 123 survey respondents, 43% agreed the activities promoted novel thinking and engagement. Narrative comments highlighted emotional impact, interdisciplinary appreciation, enjoyment, and opportunities for refinement. This feasible approach may support more observational, interpretive, and human-centered neuroscience learning.

title: Evaluation of the quantiplus rabies virus detection kit for diagnosis of rabies in humans and animals.
abstract: Rabies, a fatal zoonotic encephalitis, causes approximately 60,000 deaths annually worldwide. The current gold standard for laboratory confirmation is the direct fluorescent antibody test (DFAT) on postmortem brain samples. To overcome the limitations of DFAT, real-time PCR for rabies viral RNA detection has emerged as a reliable alternative for both antemortem and postmortem samples. This study evaluates the diagnostic performance of the Quantiplus Rabies Virus Detection Kit, a commercially available real-time PCR kit for detecting rabies RNA. The study included 24 postmortem human brain samples, 14 antemortem human samples (cerebrospinal fluid, saliva, and nuchal skin), and 44 postmortem animal brain samples. DFAT and Quantiplus assays were performed on brain samples, while Real-time TaqMan RT-PCR and Quantiplus assays were used on antemortem human samples. Using DFAT as the reference standard, the Quantiplus assay demonstrated 100% sensitivity and specificity for human and animal brain samples. It showed agreement with the in-house RT-PCR for antemortem human samples (Cohen's Kappa 1). Notwithstanding the relatively small sample size in this study, the Quantiplus assay is a reliable alternative to in-house RT-PCR for rabies diagnosis, enhancing surveillance and control efforts toward eliminating dog-mediated rabies deaths by 2030.

title: Celebrating Effort or Celebrating Outcomes? Cultural Perspectives on the USMLE and Spain's MIR.
abstract: This commentary explores how the United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) and Spain's Medical Intern Resident (MIR) examination are experienced by the community, contrasting the largely individual experience associated with the USMLE with the more communal and public celebrations observed following the MIR. Differences may reflect structural factors and broader cultural orientations toward individual versus collective achievement. Perceived social support plays a crucial role in mitigating stress and promoting well-being during medical training. Further research is needed to better understand the relationship between the cultural and social framing of examinations and outcomes such as burnout, psychological distress, and physician suicide.

title: Agreement Between Non-Invasive Type 2 Diabetes Risk Assessment Models and Associated Demographic and Socioeconomic Factors: A Cross-Sectional Study in Iranian Adults.
abstract: Non-invasive tools are recommended to identify individuals at high risk of type 2 diabetes. Agreement between validated models is unclear. This study assessed agreement between four risk-assessment models among adults attending health posts in Kerman, Iran. In this cross-sectional study, 430 adults aged≥30 years attending health posts in Kerman, Iran, were selected by multistage random sampling. Data collected by interview and examination were used to calculate FINDRISC, ModAsian FINDRISC, ADA, and AUSDRISK risk scores. Agreement was assessed with Cohen's kappa; logistic regression identified correlates of discordant classification. Agreement between AUSDRISK and ADA was poor (kappa=-0.06, 95% CI -0.07 to -0.05, P<0.001); 45.1% were high-risk by AUSDRISK but low-risk by ADA. Discordant high-risk individuals were younger, with higher BMI and waist circumference, lower physical activity, lower fruit/vegetable intake, and more hyperglycaemia. Waist circumference, male sex, and employment independently predicted discordance. Agreement between FINDRISC and ModAsian FINDRISC was moderate (kappa=0.536, 95% CI 0.48-0.60, P<0.001); 65.3% were classified into the same category by both tools, with most discordance reflecting ModAsian FINDRISC assigning a higher category than FINDRISC. Male sex was the strongest independent predictor of discordance between these two tools; BMI and low socioeconomic status were not statistically significant. Agreement between these tools was poor to moderate and varied by demographic context, indicating a need for population-based calibration. As no glycaemic outcome was measured, this study cannot establish predictive accuracy; prospective validation and calibration studies are needed to determine the most appropriate model.

title: Student Perceptions of Formative Clinical Feedback During Clerkships.
abstract: The clerkship phase of medical school is essential to the development of clinical skills necessary for medical practice. This phase depends heavily on formative feedback to help students recognize and address their strengths and weaknesses. Recent student evaluation of formative clinical feedback at Saint Louis University revealed a potential barrier in student implementation of feedback due to negative perceptions of the accuracy and utility of the formative feedback they received. Using Norcini et al.'s Consensus Framework for Good Assessment, we developed a survey to investigate the medical student perception of our institution's current system of formative feedback. Participants included 300 students in their third and fourth year medical students who had completed the clerkship phase. Response patterns indicated that, across years, Feasibility was rated highest and Catalytic Effect was rated lowest. Additionally, the only item rated higher than neutral was Feasibility, whereas Catalytic Effect, Equivalence, Acceptability, and Consistency were rated significantly below neutral. The patterns of results indicate (1) the practicality of the current formative feedback survey format and (2) students' reduced perception of the usefulness of the formative clinical feedback they receive. While this student perception is subjective in nature, it is a key metric to consider as perception has the potential to drive behavioral change. Other medical schools can consider examining their process and student perception of formative feedback using a framework of assessment similar to the Norcini framework to promote continuous quality improvement in undergraduate medical education.

title: Inhibition of TYK2 attenuates hyper IL-6- and Oncostatin M-mediated Calcium Signalling in Sensory Neurons.
journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterised by chronic pain, a debilitating symptom for which effective treatments are few and far between. IBD pathogenesis includes the prevalence of a variety of pro-inflammatory cytokines, including the Interleukin-6 (IL-6) family members Il-6 and Oncostatin M (OSM). Previous research has shown disruption of OSM signaling can modulate nociceptor sensitization and activation, however the downstream signalling pathway is unknown. When an in silico analysis of murine colonic sensory neuronal populations was undertaken for receptor expression for OSM and other factors necessary for intracellular signaling, we can find diverse expression indicative of functional signaling. We were able to observe that hyper Il-6 (Il-6 bound to the soluble Il-6 receptor) and OSM can elicit activation of a subset of murine sensory neurons by finding an increase in calcium mobilization following superfusion. This could then be attenuated by the pharmacologic inhibition of all janus kinases or interestingly, TYK2 alone. Furthermore, inhibition of transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 or transient receptor potential ankyrin 1 ion channels, which are known to be sensitized by OSM in other sensory neurons, also reduced the proportion of OSM-responsive neurons. This further understanding of OSM signaling in sensory neurons creates avenues for more extensive research into the molecular mechanisms occurring as well as the potential to exploit these therapeutically to induce analgesia in a subset of neurons.

title: Neural correlates of perceptual biases in duration perception.
abstract: How we perceive a current event depends not only on its immediate context, but also on how our internal expectations are shaped by prior experience. In time perception, these expectations manifest as systematic biases, namely sequential dependence, where the current percept is influenced by the previous stimulus, and central tendency, the overestimation of short durations and underestimation of long ones. Both perceptual biases, corresponding to individual beliefs about stimulus generation, can vary substantially between participants. However, the neural responses related to inter-individual differences in these biases remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate this question in a duration reproduction task. Our EEG results show that in the frontocentral region, the Contingent Negative Variation (CNV) while experiencing the current stimulus depends on the previous stimulus regardless of sequential dependence. In contrast, in the right parietal region, the slow potential was not influenced by previous duration but associated with inter-individual differences in sequential dependence. Stimulus-offset evoked P2 amplitude was associated with both central tendency and sequential dependence and P2 amplitude varied with previous stimulus duration depending on individual sequential dependence. A Bayesian model of time perception reproduced the observed neural dynamics of the frontocentral CNV and its dependence on previous stimulus duration, suggesting that individual internal time estimates and expectations of stimulus offset are reflected in EEG responses. Our results demonstrate that both forms of perceptual bias are reflected in neural activity while experiencing the ongoing stimulus, suggesting that neural processes related to perceptual biases directly affect the measurement of time.

title: Multiple Muscles Respond Differently to the Same Dual-Network Motor Neuron Activity.
abstract: Coordination between central pattern generator (CPG) networks underlies coordination of related rhythmic behaviors (e.g., mastication, respiration). This includes individual neurons periodically expressing activity related to more than one behavior. Here, we investigated whether muscles involved in different behaviors respond broadly to dual-network activity, or are biased toward their primary network input. We used the pyloric ("fast": ∼1 Hz: filtering of food) and gastric mill ("slow": ∼0.1 Hz: chewing) networks in the crab, Cancer borealis. During the modulatory state elicited by the neuropeptide Gly1-SIFamide, the pyloric-only lateral posterior gastric (LPG) neuron switches to dual pyloric and gastric mill network participation, enabling its contributions to inter-network coordination. LPG innervates pyloric (p7) and gastric mill (gm3b,c) muscles. Using intracellular muscle fiber recordings, we found that p7 responded to single LPG stimuli whereas gm3 required bursts to generate measurable responses. Naturalistic or fixed-parameter dual-network stimulations elicited similar peak p7 amplitudes for both network components. In contrast, gm3 primarily responded to longer-duration, slower-frequency gastric mill bursts. There were reciprocal interactions between the p7 pyloric and gastric mill responses, whereas it was unidirectional in gm3. The inter-network influences in p7 are likely due to activity-dependent synaptic plasticity which we found occurring at multiple time scales, but this was difficult to assess in gm3. Thus, interactions at the motor network level can be translated to electrical responses of muscles. However, the activity of some, but not all, muscles may be tuned to a primary behavior, even for muscles innervated by the same motor neuron.

title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Effects on Food-Related Cognition: A Cognitive Neuroscience Framework.
journal: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have transformed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity by reducing appetite, cravings and caloric intake. Growing evidence suggests effects on the central nervous system, with cognitive and neuroprotective benefits that cannot be explained by weight loss or glycaemic control alone. However, the underlying neurocognitive mechanisms remain unclear. This review proposes a cognitive neuroscience framework for investigating the effects of GLP-1RAs across multiple levels of food-related information processing. Theoretical models and experimental paradigms are integrated to dissociate perceptual, attentional, motivational, semantic and executive components. The model identifies four levels: (1) early perceptual processing, in which the brain extracts properties including caloric content and transformation; (2) attentional capture and motivational salience, which determine priorities and wanting; (3) semantic organisation, which integrates sensory and functional characteristics of foods and (4) decision-making and executive control, including inhibitory control and effort allocation. GLP-1RAs may differentially modulate these levels, which can be investigated using specific experimental paradigms. This cognitive neuroscience-based approach goes beyond descriptive measures to identify the mechanisms through which GLP-1RAs influence perception, motivation and food decisions. This framework can guide future studies, improve the interpretation of cognitive effects and contribute to the development of more targeted interventions.

title: Multiple Sclerosis in Patients Over 50: Immunosenescence, Comorbidities, and the Role of Cladribine Tablets.
abstract: The treatment of multiple sclerosis (MS) in older patients is complicated by the confluence of frailty, immunosenescence, and comorbidities. With advancing age, the immune system undergoes significant changes that progressively limit its ability to mount effective responses, with a reduction of naïve lymphocytes and the accumulation of senescent T and B cells. Additionally, elderly individuals with MS tend to have a higher burden of comorbidities, which can further complicate therapeutic decision-making. In the elderly MS population, the use of aggressive immunosuppressive strategies is associated with an increased risk of infections and reduced vaccine responsiveness, and may therefore pose additional risks as compared to the younger population. This narrative review explores how immunosenescence and comorbidities need to be taken into account when choosing the most appropriate treatment. Particular attention is given to immune reconstitution therapies (IRTs), with a focus on cladribine tablets (CladT), as a possible treatment strategy in this population. A targeted literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE to identify relevant studies published up to October 2025, using combinations of terms covering multiple sclerosis, aging, older adults, immunosenescence, frailty, comorbidities, disease-modifying therapies, and cladribine. The evidence was synthesized narratively, with particular attention to the level of evidence and its applicability to older or frail patients. CladT may represent one potential therapeutic option in selected patients, as the drug is characterized by transient immune suppression followed by immune recovery. This mechanism may enable disease control while limiting continuous exposure to treatment. Clinical trials and real-world data suggest that CladT has a generally manageable safety profile and may be effective in reducing relapse rates and disability progression across age groups, although evidence in older and frail populations remains limited. In older patients, therapeutic decisions should balance treatment efficacy against the heightened risks associated with immunosenescence, comorbidities, and frailty, rather than relying on chronological age alone. Within this framework, CladT - owing to its intermittent dosing and reduced continuous immunosuppression - may be relevant in selected patients, although direct evidence in older and frail populations remains limited. An individualized approach to MS treatment in older patients is required, integrating considerations related to immunosenescence, comorbidities, and frailty. In this context, CladT may be considered among the available therapeutic options in selected patients, although further evidence in older populations is needed.

title: Cervical 3D-kinematics, muscle-properties and pain in fast-jet pilots versus non-pilots.
abstract: Fast-jet pilots frequently experience high +Gz forces, leading to cervical musculoskeletal adaptations and performance impairments. The biomechanical mechanisms underlying these effects remain unclear. Understanding these biomechanical adaptations is critical to developing preventive measures and ergonomic guidelines aimed at reducing the risk of injury, maintaining pilot health and ensuring long-term operational readiness, and ultimately improving flight safety. This study compared cervical muscle properties, kinematics and movement-related pain perception between fast-jet pilots and matched non-pilot controls. Twenty Eurofighter pilots and 20 near-matched non-pilots participated in a cross-sectional comparative study. Muscle tone, stiffness and elasticity were measured using MyotonPRO. Cervical movements were analysed via 3D motion capture. Pain was measured by the Visual Analogue Scale. Statistical group comparisons were performed. No significant differences in cervical range of motion between groups were found (P > 0.05). Pilots exhibited reduced elasticity in the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles (P 0.05). Pilots maintain normal cervical mobility, compared to non-pilots, despite high-G exposure, but altered muscle properties suggest long-term adaptations. Occupational medicine approaches, including ergonomic cockpit adjustments, targeted physiotherapy, and preventive exercise protocols, are recommended to address cervical muscle adaptations identified in this study. Such strategies could mitigate musculoskeletal strain, enhance pilot wellbeing, and sustain operational safety throughout pilots' careers.

title: Frontal Cerebral Blood Flow Deficits in Behavioral Variant Frontotemporal Dementia: Associations With Clinical Symptoms, Peripheral Vascular Biomarkers, and Neuroimaging Measures.
abstract: This study aimed to characterize regional cerebral blood flow (CBF) alterations in behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), examine their associations with clinical symptoms and peripheral vascular/synaptic biomarkers, evaluate spatial concordance with gray matter volume (GMV) loss and glucose hypometabolism, and explore CBF's mediating role between biomarkers and clinical outcomes. Thirty-five bvFTD patients and 27 matched normal controls (NC) underwent clinical assessments, ASL MRI, 18F-FDG PET, and structural MRI. Plasma vascular (VEGFA, PDGF-BB) and synaptic (NPTXR, NPTX2) biomarkers were measured via the Olink platform. Statistical analyses included group comparisons, ROC analysis, multiple linear regression, and mediation analysis. Compared with normal controls, bvFTD patients exhibited significantly reduced CBF in both frontal and temporal regions, which showed regional spatial concordance with GMV and FDG uptake in corresponding areas. Frontal CBF demonstrated good diagnostic accuracy and was significantly associated with multiple clinical measures including MMSE, MoCA, ADL, and behavioral scales, as well as with peripheral vascular and synaptic biomarkers. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested statistical indirect associations linking peripheral vascular biomarkers to clinical symptoms through frontal CBF and linking frontal CBF to behavioral outcomes through frontal GMV. BvFTD is characterized by frontotemporal hypoperfusion, with frontal CBF closely associated with cognitive, behavioral, and functional impairment. The regional concordance of ASL-derived CBF with gray matter atrophy and glucose hypometabolism supports its potential role as an accessible, non-invasive, and radiation-free complementary neuroimaging biomarker. The mediation findings should be considered hypothesis-generating because they did not remain significant after FDR correction and require validation in larger longitudinal studies.

title: Electroacupuncture May Alleviate Depression and Exerts Anti-Inflammatory Effects Through IDO1 Modulation of the Kynurenine Pathway.
abstract: Depression is one of the most common mental health conditions worldwide. Numerous studies have identified various factors associated with the onset of depression. Among these factors, inflammation is a key contributor. During the inflammatory process, pro-inflammatory cytokines activate indole-2,3-dioxygenase (IDO), which converts tryptophan (TRP) to kynurenine (KYN) via the KYN pathway (KP). This increases the production of neurotoxic byproducts, thereby exacerbating depressive symptoms. Studies have shown that electroacupuncture (EA) has anti-inflammatory and antidepressant properties. The present study aimed to investigate the effects of EA on depression and its mechanisms of action via IDO1 and the KP. An inflammation-induced depression mouse model was created by injecting lipopolysaccharide (LPS) intraperitoneally. After the model was successfully established, the Hegu (L14) and Taichong (LR3) acupoints were treated with EA at a frequency of 15 Hz and an intensity of 0.3 mA for 45 min. A subset of mice received ketamine as an antidepressant intervention. The following assessments were performed: open-field test (OFT), sucrose preference test (SPT), forced swim test (FST), and tail suspension test (TST). An enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was used to measure IDO1 levels and related inflammatory factors in brain tissue and peripheral blood. High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) was used to measure KP metabolism-related metabolite levels. Quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) was used to measure IDO1 and inflammation-related factor levels. LPS significantly induced depression-like behavior in mice. Ketamine effectively alleviated this behavior, exerting an antidepressant effect and suppressing IDO1 expression, as well as the levels of inflammatory factors (IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6). Following EA intervention, depression-like behavior in mice with LPS-induced depression was alleviated. EA effectively reduced peripheral and central inflammatory factor expression levels and suppressed IDO1 expression. EA alleviated depressive symptoms in mice by modulating the IDO1-mediated KP. EA effectively reduced the expression of inflammatory factors, alleviated LPS-induced depressive-like behavior, and improved depressive symptoms by modulating the IDO1-mediated KP.

title: Biological and epigenetic pathways linking PTSD to accelerated aging: a systematic review and narrative synthesis.
abstract: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) may accelerate biological aging, but the pathways and evidence remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed associations between PTSD and epigenetic and other aging biomarkers. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus through 1 March 2026 for studies of adults with validated PTSD assessment. Two reviewers screened records and extracted data. Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Findings were synthesized narratively because study designs and outcomes were heterogeneous. Twenty-four studies including 512,768 participants met the inclusion criteria. Twenty-two (91.7%) reported positive associations between PTSD and accelerated biological aging across epigenetic clocks, telomere length, and transcriptional measures; GrimAge acceleration ranged from 1.83 to 2.53 years in veterans. Epigenome-wide association study findings implicated immune- and inflammation-related genes. Longitudinal and twin studies supported temporal precedence and partial independence from genetic confounding. However, 79.2% of studies were United States-based, 45.8% involved military or veteran samples, and most were cross-sectional, limiting generalizability and causal inference. PTSD is associated with faster biological aging across several biomarkers, but diverse longitudinal and intervention studies are needed before causality or reversibility can be established. More diverse long-term studies and treatment trials areneeded before these measures can guide routine care.

title: Epigenetics and the personalized treatment of anxiety disorders.
abstract: Anxiety disorders are to be treated with cognitive behavioral therapy and serotonergic antidepressants. Clinical aspects are to be taken into account in an individualized approach. To further develop personalized, biomarker-based treatments neuroscience research has focused on brain imaging, laboratory markers, genetics and epigenetics. The current review focuses on research on how epigenetic variation affects therapy outcome. It summarizes the literature which comprises 12 studies focusing on the role of DNA methylation with few replicated findings between studies. Results are summarized and interpreted in context with genetic findings. Methodological limitations of epigenetic studies are discussed. First, cohort sizes are small compared to those used in genetic studies. Second, preanalytical procedures are of particular importance in epigenetic research because of the inherent instability of DNA methylation; generally accepted standard protocols are currently lacking. Third, the transferability of blood methylation status to brain or liver has to be addressed in interpretation of the results. Solutions to address these methodological challenges are discussed focusing on a synergistic approach with genetic studies. The development of a consensus on standards of epigenetic methodology will be essential to allow the realization of its potential for a personalized treatment of anxiety disorders.

title: A Belgian study assessing relapsing multiple sclerosis activity through automated magnetic resonance imaging volumetry.
abstract: This study assessed to what extent icobrain ms, a commercially available artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) volumetry software, detected disease activity in patients with clinically and radiologically stable relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS), and estimated its impact on radiologists' assessments. We retrospectively enrolled 111 RMS patients with two consecutive MRI scans at one year interval, without relapses, progression or radiological changes while remaining on stable therapy. MRI scans were analyzed by four radiologists acting independently, and by icobrain ms. The radiologists performed their assessments both without and with icobrain ms support and categorized patient status based on lesion and brain volume changes. Radiologists' detection of lesion activity non-significantly increased from 6.8% to 8.6% (McNemar p = 0.215; ordinal regression p = 0.06; sign-test p = 0.08) using icobrain ms. Detection of accelerated brain volume loss increased from 2.0% to 7.7% (all p < 0.01). Inter-reader agreement improved from 36% to 56% for lesions, and from 26% to 40% for brain loss (Kendall's W, p < 0.001). Icobrain ms detected new or significantly enlarged lesions in 16.2% and accelerated brain volume loss in 6.3% of participants. AI-assisted MRI volumetry may support radiologists to detect subclinical disease activity in patients characterized as having stable disease.

title: The efficacy and safety of lurasidone in adolescents with bipolar disorder: a up-to-date drug profile.
abstract: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a psychiatric condition characterized by recurrent episodes of mania or hypomania and depression, impairing psychosocial functioning across-the-lifespan. Pharmacotherapy in youths current includes mood-stabilizers (lithium) and several second/third‑generation antipsychotics (SGAs). Lurasidone (LUR) is a therapeutic, approved by FDA, for the treatment of bipolar depression in youths aged 10 years and older. The authors review the current evidence from published literature on the main pharmacological features of LUR in adolescents with BD. The authors review the efficacy and short- and long-term safety in bipolar adolescents is critically reviewed. Information is also provided on dosing, combinations, the management of side-effects (nausea, akathisia, sedation), along with details on switching to other alternative SGAs and its possible discontinuation after enduring improvement. Although LUR and olanzapine-fluoxetine combination are the only FDA-approved medications for pediatric bipolar depression, LUR shows promise as a first-line treatment, due to its lower risk of weight gain and metabolic disturbances, and possible effectiveness on neurocognitive dysfunctions of early-onset BD. However, considering our understanding of its efficacy is based on a single RCT, further investigation is warranted. In terms of its long-term safety, currently available safety data suggest that LUR is a good option also for maintenance treatments. However, given that tolerability can change over time, close monitoring is also recommended.

title: Development, Optimization, and Physicochemical Characterization of Fluorescent Carbon Dot-Ginkgo biloba Extract Co-Loaded Niosomes for Future Neurological Disease-Relevant Evaluation.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is one of the major neurodegenerative diseases that affect the human brain and lead to memory loss. The present approaches to disease management have been relatively poor; the therapies provided do not arrest the disease process. This study aimed to develop and optimize dual-loaded niosomes containing Ginkgo biloba extract and CDOTs and to evaluate their physicochemical properties, formulation-level fluorescence, in vitro release, and preliminary cytocompatibility. The study did not assess blood-brain barrier transport, neuronal effects, Alzheimer's disease-specific mechanisms, or in vivo therapeutic efficacy. Niosomes were prepared based on non-ionic surfactants and cholesterol for the encapsulation of Ginkgo and CDOTs. The response surface methodology (RSM) was used to optimize niosomal formulations through a Box-Behnken design. The formulations were evaluated for vesicle size, entrapment efficiency, and release profile. Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM) research indicated that the average diameters of the free niosomes and CDOT@Ginkgo@Niosomes were 69.56 nm and 72.19 nm, respectively. HFF cell viability remained high at lower concentrations, whereas significant reductions in viability were observed at 10 and 50 μg/mL after 48 h, indicating concentration-dependent cytocompatibility. The formulation exhibited acceptable preliminary cytocompatibility at lower concentrations, whereas reduced viability was observed at higher concentrations. For both CDOT and Ginkgo, CDOT@Ginkgo@Niosomes showed a delayed release profile over 72 h, with near-complete release observed at the final time point. CDOT@Ginkgo@Niosomes showed successful co-loading, preserved formulation-level fluorescence, delayed release, and acceptable cytocompatibility at lower concentrations in HFF cells. These findings support further formulation optimization and subsequent evaluation in disease-relevant neuronal, blood-brain barrier, and in vivo models. The present results do not demonstrate neuroprotection, diagnostic performance, blood-brain barrier transport, or the prevention or treatment of neurodegenerative disease.

title: Beyond the Microbial Hypothesis: Shared Genetic, Osteoimmune and Vascular Mechanisms in the Oral-Brain Axis Linking Periodontitis and Alzheimer's Disease.
abstract: Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease of the tooth-supporting tissues, is increasingly linked to Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet mechanistic accounts of this 'oral-brain axis' have been dominated by microbial translocation and the gingipain hypothesis. This review argues that the convergence between periodontitis and AD extends well beyond microbes, integrating shared genetic, osteoimmune and vascular-inflammatory mechanisms that are rarely considered together. Genetic susceptibility reaches beyond APOE ε4 to the osteoprotegerin (OPG) axis, with APOE ε4 linking the two conditions through impaired amyloid-β clearance, blood-brain barrier dysfunction and altered lipid handling. The OPG/RANK/RANKL system emerges as a bone-brain (osteoimmune) interface, in which OPG shows a dual-role paradox, reduced locally in periodontal bone loss yet elevated systematically in AD, while soluble RANKL displays neuroprotective properties. Because OPG acts as a decoy receptor for RANKL, we hypothesise that elevated OPG in AD limits RANKL-dependent microglial amyloid-β clearance. Endothelial dysfunction, reflected in circulating endocan, provides a shared vascular readout that is raised in both diseases and responsive to periodontal therapy. We propose that these genetic, microbial and vascular inputs converge on microglial priming and trained immunity, a unifying immunological node through which chronic peripheral inflammation may act during the decades-long preclinical phase of AD. Current evidence nonetheless remains predominantly associative, causality is unproven and mechanistic data rely heavily on animal models. The oral-brain axis is therefore best regarded as a promising yet still unproven framework in which osteoimmune and vascular pathways, and candidate biomarkers such as endocan, represent underexplored targets for future longitudinal and interventional research.

title: Investigating the Effect of RACZ Epidural Neuroplasty With Ozone Injection in Patients With Chronic Radicular Lumbar Pain: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
abstract: Although the exact causes of chronic lumbar radicular pain are still unknown, potential causes include epidural fibrosis, arachnoiditis, mechanical failure, nerve root inflammation, and structural and degenerative changes to the spine. This study was conducted to assess the analgesic effect of using epidural ozone injection along with routine RACZ neuroplasty in patients with low back pain. This is a prospective randomized clinical trial conducted on 40 patients with chronic radicular lumbar pain allocated into two equal groups of RACZ caudal neuroplasty with and without ozone injection. Two groups of twenty people each were created from forty patients with chronic radicular lumbar pain who did not improve with conservative measures. In Group B, RACZ neuroplasty was performed, while in Group A, RACZ neuroplasty was administered along with epidural ozone injection. Before the intervention, baseline pain intensity and the degree of back pain-related disability were determined using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), respectively. Twenty-four hours, 1 month, and 3 months after the procedure, the NRS was recorded again. ODI was also assessed 1 month and 3 months after the procedure. The mean NRS scores in the intervention group before, and 24 h, 1 month, and 3 months after the procedure were 8.80 ± 1.47, 4.45 ± 2.01, 5.25 ± 1.25, and 5.40 ± 2.16, respectively, and corresponding values in the control group were 8.70 ± 1.30, 4.60 ± 1.60, 5.70 ± 1.66, and 6.40 ± 1.64, respectively (Group effect: F = 0.784, p = 0.381 and Time effect: F = 81.910, p < 0.001). The mean scores of the ODI before, 1 month, and 3 months after the procedure were 48.60 ± 17.65, 40.75 ± 15.38, and 43.70 ± 18.50, respectively, in the intervention group, while in the control group, the respective values were 57.20 ± 15.67, 43.90 ± 19.92, and 48.75 ± 12.83. (Group effect: F = 1.246, p = 0.271 and Time effect: F = 24.496, p < 0.001). While the addition of ozone to RACZ neuroplasty showed no significant benefit in this study, these findings are limited by the modest sample size and short follow-up. Further large-scale, well-powered trials are required to definitively establish the therapeutic role of ozone in this population. Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT): IRCT20150724023315N3.

title: Persisting psychological complications following the use of classic psychedelics: A qualitative study of help-seeking experiences.
abstract: While growing enthusiasm for the therapeutic potential of classic psychedelics has led to a rise in non-clinical use, attention to persisting adverse effects has emerged with delay. A subset of individuals report persisting complications such as hallucinogen persisting perception disorder (HPPD), depersonalization/derealization disorder (DDD), anxiety and depression. Yet few medical services are equipped to address these complications. This qualitative study examines how societal, medical, and media discourses shape the experiences of individuals with persisting psychedelic-related complications, focusing on help-seeking trajectories. Thirteen semi-structured interviews with adults experiencing persisting psychedelic-related psychological symptoms (four women, nine men, age 19-49 years; HPPD (n = 10), DDD (n = 6), depression (n = 1), and anxiety (n = 1)) were conducted within a larger study on these complications. All psychedelic index experiences preceding the onset of symptoms occurred in non-clinical, naturalistic settings rather than in controlled clinical or research contexts. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Reporting followed the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research (COREQ) guidelines. Three interrelated themes emerged: (1) The dissonance between expectation and harm-idealized media and scientific portrayals of psychedelics shaped initial use and complicated recognition of adverse outcomes; (2) stigma, silence, and self-blame-prohibitionist discourse and internalized shame significantly inhibited help-seeking; and (3) between systemic absence and self-organized support-participants encountered clinical unpreparedness and epistemic dismissal, which often led them to rely on online peer communities and self-management strategies. Positive clinical encounters, characterized by professional expertise and non-judgemental engagement, were experienced as helpful. Adequate clinical and conceptual frameworks for persisting psychedelic-related complications are lacking. An interdisciplinary, experience-informed approach integrating realistic risk communication, clinician training, and destigmatization is required to support affected individuals.

title: Paratonia Is More than Hypertonia: From Facilitation to Motor Response Inhibition.
Unravelling the Chemolithoautotrophic Metabolism of the Carboxydotrophic Knallgas Bacterium Hydrogenophaga pseudoflava.
abstract: The sustainable production of chemicals is critical to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and environmental pollution. Gaseous feedstocks from industrial waste streams and waste gasification, including CO, CO2 and H2, represent abundant and underutilized resources for biotechnology. Syngas fermentation has been predominantly studied under anaerobic conditions, whereas aerobic processes may offer advantages for the biosynthesis of energy-intensive products. One promising organism is the aerobic carboxydotroph Hydrogenophaga pseudoflava DSM 1084, whose chemolithoautotrophic metabolism remains poorly understood. To address this, we performed proteome analysis under different growth conditions and characterized deletion mutants of key enzymes involved in CO and H2 oxidation. Deletion mutants showed that only CO dehydrogenase I and the membrane-bound hydrogenase are essential for CO and H2 oxidation, respectively. The role of the putative second CO dehydrogenase remains to be elucidated, and the soluble hydrogenase may contribute to redox balancing under microaerobic or anaerobic conditions. In addition, the H2-sensing regulatory system appears to be nonfunctional, and the transhydrogenase PntAB supports redox homeostasis during chemolithoautotrophic growth. Electrons from CO or H2 are transferred via the reduced quinone pool to NADH through proton-motive force-driven reverse electron transfer. Nevertheless, growth on CO remains slower than on CO2/H2. In contrast to CO2/H2, an unphysiologically high CO concentration (80%) led to a major proteome rearrangement, with 1879 of 3640 reliably quantified proteins showing altered abundance compared to fructose-grown cells, including a pronounced stress response. Under such conditions, cells are likely to invest additional energy to maintain redox balance. Together with the less energy-conserving autotrophic branch of the respiratory chain and cytoplasmic CO oxidation, this results in inefficient CO conversion and reduced growth.

title: Brain Transcriptomic Changes Associated With the Socially Regulated Behavioural Specialisation of Ant Queens.
abstract: Insect societies are characterised by a reproductive division of labour between queens that monopolise egg production and workers that perform all non-reproductive tasks. The queen specialisation in egg laying is typically considered to be constitutive and independent of environmental conditions, but this common assumption was recently challenged by the finding that the presence of workers both induces and maintains the queen specialisation in several species of ants. However, the molecular changes that translate worker presence into queen behavioural specialisation remain unknown. To investigate the transcriptomic basis of the socially regulated specialisation of ant queens, we produced 93 individual brain transcriptomes from queens of the black garden ant Lasius niger that were experimentally maintained in different social environments. Our transcriptomic analyses revealed that 123 genes were differentially expressed between the brains of queens maintained with and without workers. These genes were enriched for processes related to brain energy metabolism and neuronal plasticity and signalling. By investigating the response of selected genes of interest to further manipulations of the social environment, we identified four candidate genes that fully mirrored the queen behavioural changes. Specifically, their expression changes in response to worker presence were reversible and they did not respond to mere cues of the worker presence. These candidate genes included the transcription factor Krüppel-homologue 1 and other genes in the juvenile hormone and insulin signalling pathways, both known to regulate multiple aspects of division of labour in social insects. By producing a robust, well-replicated and well-controlled investigation of the transcriptomic basis of the behavioural specialisation of ant queens, this study provides a better understanding of the emergence and maintenance of reproductive division of labour in insect societies.

title: Neonatal stress is associated with region-specific changes in mitochondrial respiration and sex-dependent respiratory instability in adulthood.
abstract: Early-life stress is increasingly recognized as a critical determinant of brain development, yet its long-term impact on the neural control of breathing remains poorly defined. Here we show that neonatal maternal separation (NMS, P3-P12) induces long-term alterations in respiratory stability and mitochondrial function within respiratory circuits. In adulthood, NMS altered respiratory stability, with significant treatment × sex interactions for total and postsigh apnoeas; post hoc comparisons showed increased frequencies of these apnoeic events in males. Sigh frequency also showed a significant main effect of treatment. Region-specific high-resolution respirometry showed that NMS was associated with reduced mitochondrial respiration in the paraventricular hypothalamus (PVH) and increased mitochondrial respiration in the nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) and ventral respiratory column (VRC), without significant treatment × sex interactions. Normalization to cytochrome c oxidase (COX) activity largely eliminated these differences, suggesting that changes in absolute respiration are consistent with a contribution of differences in mitochondrial content rather than major alterations in respiratory capacity relative to mitochondrial abundance. In the pre-Bötzinger complex, absolute mitochondrial respiration was preserved, whereas oxygen consumption rate (OCR)/COX ratios revealed treatment-dependent alterations in mitochondrial respiratory flux relative to mitochondrial content. NMS also altered the expression of selected genes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis, mitophagy, fusion and fission in the NTS and VRC, with significant main effects of treatment and sex but no treatment × sex interactions. Oxidative and inflammatory markers were largely preserved, although selective effects of sex and treatment were detected. Together, these findings demonstrate that neonatal stress produces persistent, region-specific remodelling of mitochondrial and molecular pathways within respiratory circuits, accompanied by sex-dependent vulnerability to respiratory instability. KEY POINTS: Early-life stress induces a persistent, sex-dependent disruption of respiratory control, increasing apnoeas in adult males, whereas females remain comparatively resistant. This phenotype is associated with region-specific remodelling of mitochondrial function along the paraventricular hypothalamus (PVH)-brainstem axis, characterized by reduced hypothalamic respiration and increased brainstem mitochondrial respiration after neonatal stress.
